lessons.title: Exercise 1.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A rational expression is p(x)/q(x) where p(x) and q(x) are polynomials and q(x) is not zero.
  • Any polynomial can be written over 1, for example x + 1 = (x + 1)/1, so it behaves like a rational number.
  • In a polynomial, the exponent of the variable in every term must be zero or a positive integer.
  • Terms such as 3/x = 3x^(-1) or 1/x = x^(-1) have negative powers, so expressions containing them as written are not polynomials.
  • A square root such as √(x + 1) = (x + 1)^(1/2) is not a polynomial because 1/2 is not a positive integer.
  • The constant 2 is a rational expression because it can be written as 2/1, with 2 and 1 constant polynomials.
  • The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable in it.
  • A non-zero constant such as 5 has degree 0, because 5 = 5x^0.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Which expressions behave like rational numbers? x + 1

Ans: A rational expression p(x)/q(x), q(x) not zero, behaves like a rational number.
x + 1 can be written as (x + 1)/1, where x + 1 and 1 are polynomials.
So x + 1 behaves like a rational number.

Q: Q1 (ii). (x² + 1)/(x − 1)

Ans: Here p(x) = x² + 1 and q(x) = x − 1 are both polynomials and q(x) is not zero.
So (x² + 1)/(x − 1) is of the form p(x)/q(x).
It behaves like a rational number.

Q: Q1 (iii). x² + 3/x

Ans: The term 3/x contains x with power −1.
So x² + 3/x is not a polynomial, and the expression is not of the form p(x)/q(x) as written.
It does not behave like a rational number.

Q: Q1 (iv). (x² + 2x + 3)/(x² + 2)

Ans: Here p(x) = x² + 2x + 3 and q(x) = x² + 2 are both polynomials and q(x) is not zero.
So the expression is of the form p(x)/q(x).
It behaves like a rational number.

Q: Q1 (v). (x³ + 2x² + 3x + 1)/(x² + 4x + 5)

Ans: Here p(x) = x³ + 2x² + 3x + 1 and q(x) = x² + 4x + 5 are both polynomials and q(x) is not zero.
So the expression is of the form p(x)/q(x).
It behaves like a rational number.

Q: Q2 (i). Which expressions are polynomials? √(x + 1)

Ans: In a polynomial, the exponent of the variable in every term is zero or a positive integer.
√(x + 1) = (x + 1)^(1/2), and 1/2 is not a positive integer.
So √(x + 1) is not a polynomial.

Q: Q2 (ii). x² + 2x + 3

Ans: The exponents of x in the terms are 2, 1 and 0.
All are zero or positive integers.
So x² + 2x + 3 is a polynomial.

Q: Q2 (iii). x² − 1/x + 1

Ans: 1/x = x^(−1), and −1 is not a positive integer.
So x² − 1/x + 1 is not a polynomial.

Q: Q2 (iv). 8x²y + 5xy

Ans: In each term the exponents of x and y are positive integers.
So 8x²y + 5xy is a polynomial.

Q: Q2 (v). x³ − 1/(2x²) + 3/4

Ans: 1/(2x²) contains x with power −2, which is not a positive integer.
So x³ − 1/(2x²) + 3/4 is not a polynomial.

Q: Q3 (i). Which of the following are rational expressions? (x² + x + 3)/(x³ + 1)

Ans: p(x) = x² + x + 3 and q(x) = x³ + 1 are both polynomials, and q(x) is not zero.
So (x² + x + 3)/(x³ + 1) is a rational expression.

Q: Q3 (ii). (x³ + 4/x + 2)/(x² + 1)

Ans: The numerator x³ + 4/x + 2 contains 4/x = 4x^(−1).
So the numerator is not a polynomial.
Hence the expression is not a rational expression.

Q: Q3 (iii). √(x² + 3) − 1

Ans: The expression contains the square root of a polynomial, so it cannot be written as p(x)/q(x) with p(x), q(x) polynomials.
It is not a rational expression.

Q: Q3 (iv). 1/x

Ans: 1/x = p(x)/q(x) with p(x) = 1 and q(x) = x, both polynomials, q(x) not zero.
So 1/x is a rational expression.

Q: Q3 (v). 2

Ans: 2 can be written as 2/1, where 2 and 1 are constant polynomials.
So 2 is a rational expression.

Q: Q3 (vi). 3/(x³ − 1)

Ans: p(x) = 3 and q(x) = x³ − 1 are both polynomials, and q(x) is not zero.
So 3/(x³ − 1) is a rational expression.

Q: Q4 (i). Find the degree of the polynomial: x³ + 2x² + 3x + 4

Ans: The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable in it.
The highest power of x here is 3.
Degree = 3.

Q: Q4 (ii). x² + 2x + 3

Ans: The highest power of x is 2.
Degree = 2.

Q: Q4 (iii). (1/3)x + 4

Ans: The highest power of x is 1.
Degree = 1.

Q: Q4 (iv). 5

Ans: 5 is a constant polynomial, i.e. 5 = 5x⁰.
The highest power of x is 0.
Degree = 0.

Q: Q4 (v). −2x² + (5/3)x + 4

Ans: The highest power of x is 2.
Degree = 2.

mcqs.q: Which expression behaves like a rational number?
mcqs.why: x + 1 can be written as (x + 1)/1, where the numerator x + 1 and the denominator 1 are both polynomials and the denominator is not zero, so it is of the form p(x)/q(x).

mcqs.q: Does (x² + 1)/(x − 1) behave like a rational number?
options: No, because the denominator contains x
No, because the numerator has degree 2
Yes, because it cannot be simplified
Yes, because both parts are polynomials and the denominator is not zero
mcqs.why: Here p(x) = x² + 1 and q(x) = x − 1 are both polynomials, and q(x) is not zero, so the expression is exactly of the form p(x)/q(x) and behaves like a rational number.

mcqs.q: Why does x² + 3/x NOT behave like a rational number as written?
options: Because x² is not a polynomial
Because 3/x contains x with power −1, so the whole expression is not a polynomial in the required form
mcqs.why: Write 3/x as 3x^(-1). The exponent −1 is not zero or a positive integer, so x² + 3/x is not a polynomial and, as written, is not of the form p(x)/q(x) with polynomial parts.

mcqs.q: Which of these behaves like a rational number?
mcqs.why: In (x² + 2x + 3)/(x² + 2), the numerator x² + 2x + 3 and the denominator x² + 2 are both polynomials and the denominator is not zero, so it has the form p(x)/q(x).

mcqs.q: Which expression is a polynomial?
mcqs.why: In x² + 2x + 3 the exponents of x are 2, 1 and 0. All of them are zero or positive integers, which is exactly the condition for an expression to be a polynomial.

mcqs.q: Why is √(x + 1) not a polynomial?
options: Because it has no constant term
Because it has only one term
Because √(x + 1) = (x + 1)^(1/2) and 1/2 is not a positive integer exponent
Because x + 1 is not a polynomial
mcqs.why: A polynomial needs every exponent of the variable to be zero or a positive integer. Rewriting the root gives exponent 1/2, which fails that condition, so √(x + 1) is not a polynomial.

mcqs.q: Which expression is NOT a polynomial?
mcqs.why: In x² − 1/x + 1, the term 1/x equals x^(-1). The exponent −1 is not a positive integer, so the whole expression cannot be a polynomial, even though its other terms are fine.

mcqs.q: 8x²y + 5xy is a polynomial because:
options: in each term the exponents of x and y are positive integers
it contains no fractions at all in any form
mcqs.why: Check each term: in 8x²y the exponents are 2 and 1, and in 5xy they are 1 and 1. Every exponent is a positive integer, so the expression satisfies the definition of a polynomial.

mcqs.q: Which expression is a rational expression?
mcqs.why: Here p(x) = x² + x + 3 and q(x) = x³ + 1 are both polynomials and q(x) is not zero, so the quotient is a rational expression. The first option fails because its numerator contains 4/x.

mcqs.q: Why is (x³ + 4/x + 2)/(x² + 1) NOT a rational expression?
options: Its numerator contains 4/x = 4x^(−1), so the numerator is not a polynomial
mcqs.why: A rational expression needs BOTH numerator and denominator to be polynomials. The term 4/x has the negative power −1, so x³ + 4/x + 2 is not a polynomial and the whole expression is not rational.

mcqs.q: Which statement about 1/x is correct?
options: It is not a rational expression
It is a rational expression, with p(x) = 1 and q(x) = x
It is a rational expression only if x = 1
mcqs.why: Write 1/x as p(x)/q(x) with p(x) = 1 and q(x) = x. Both are polynomials and q(x) is not zero, so 1/x is a rational expression, although it is not itself a polynomial.

mcqs.q: Why is the constant 2 a rational expression?
options: Because 2 can be written as 2/1, where 2 and 1 are constant polynomials
Because 2 is a polynomial of degree 2
Because every integer is a polynomial of degree 1
mcqs.why: Every constant is a constant polynomial. Writing 2 = 2/1 puts it in the form p(x)/q(x) with polynomial numerator and denominator and a non-zero denominator, so 2 is a rational expression.

mcqs.q: What is the degree of x³ + 2x² + 3x + 4?
mcqs.why: The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable appearing in it. The powers here are 3, 2, 1 and 0, and the highest of these is 3, so the degree is 3.

mcqs.q: What is the degree of the constant polynomial 5?
mcqs.why: Write the constant as 5 = 5x^0. The highest (and only) power of x is 0, so a non-zero constant polynomial always has degree 0, whatever its value.

mcqs.q: What is the degree of −2x² + (5/3)x + 4?
mcqs.why: List the powers of x: the first term has power 2, the second has power 1 and the constant has power 0. The highest power is 2, so the degree of the polynomial is 2.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A rational expression is in its lowest term when p(x) and q(x) have no common factor.
  • To reduce an expression, factorize the numerator and denominator fully, then cancel the common factors.
  • x² − 4 = (x + 2)(x − 2) by the formula a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
  • x³ + 1 = (x + 1)(x² − x + 1) by a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²), and z³ − 1 = (z − 1)(z² + z + 1) by a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).
  • (x² − x − 6)/(x + 2) reduces to x − 3, because x² − x − 6 = (x − 3)(x + 2).
  • x⁴ + 4 factorizes as (x² + 2x + 2)(x² − 2x + 2) by writing it as (x² + 2)² − (2x)² and using a² − b².

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Which of the following expressions are in their lowest term? (x + 1)/(2x − 1)

Ans: A rational expression is in its lowest term when p(x) and q(x) have no common factor.
x + 1 and 2x − 1 have no common factor.
So (x + 1)/(2x − 1) is in its lowest term.

Q: Q1 (ii). (3x² + 3)/(9x + 27)

Ans: 3x² + 3 = 3(x² + 1)
9x + 27 = 9(x + 3)
Numerator and denominator have the common factor 3.
So the expression is not in its lowest term.

Q: Q1 (iii). (x² + 3x + 2)/(x + 2)

Ans: x² + 3x + 2 = x² + x + 2x + 2
= x(x + 1) + 2(x + 1)
= (x + 1)(x + 2)
The factor (x + 2) is common with the denominator.
So the expression is not in its lowest term.

Q: Q1 (iv). (x² − 4)/(x + 2)

Ans: Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
x² − 4 = x² − 2² = (x + 2)(x − 2)
The factor (x + 2) is common with the denominator.
So the expression is not in its lowest term.

Q: Q1 (v). (4x + 8)/2

Ans: 4x + 8 = 2(2x + 4)
Numerator and denominator have the common factor 2.
So the expression is not in its lowest term.

Q: Q1 (vi). (4x² + 3)/(x + 3)

Ans: 4x² + 3 cannot be factorized, and it has no factor in common with x + 3.
So (4x² + 3)/(x + 3) is in its lowest term.

Q: Q2 (i). Reduce to lowest terms: (x² − x − 6)/(x + 2)

Ans: Factorize the numerator:
x² − x − 6 = x² − 3x + 2x − 6
= x(x − 3) + 2(x − 3)
= (x − 3)(x + 2)
So (x² − x − 6)/(x + 2) = (x − 3)(x + 2)/(x + 2)
Cancelling the common factor (x + 2):
= x − 3

Q: Q2 (ii). (x³ + 1)/(x² − 1)

Ans: Using a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²):
x³ + 1 = (x + 1)(x² − x + 1)
Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
x² − 1 = (x + 1)(x − 1)
So (x³ + 1)/(x² − 1) = (x + 1)(x² − x + 1)/((x + 1)(x − 1))
Cancelling the common factor (x + 1):
= (x² − x + 1)/(x − 1)

Q: Q2 (iii). (x²y + xy)/(xy² − xy)

Ans: x²y + xy = xy(x + 1)
xy² − xy = xy(y − 1)
So (x²y + xy)/(xy² − xy) = xy(x + 1)/(xy(y − 1))
Cancelling the common factor xy:
= (x + 1)/(y − 1)

Q: Q2 (iv). (x⁴ + 2x² + 1)/(x⁴ − 1)

Ans: x⁴ + 2x² + 1 = (x² + 1)² = (x² + 1)(x² + 1)
Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
x⁴ − 1 = (x² + 1)(x² − 1)
So (x⁴ + 2x² + 1)/(x⁴ − 1) = (x² + 1)(x² + 1)/((x² + 1)(x² − 1))
Cancelling the common factor (x² + 1):
= (x² + 1)/(x² − 1)

Q: Q2 (v). (x⁴ + 4)/(x² − 2x + 2)

Ans: x⁴ + 4 = (x² + 2)² − (2x)²
Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
x⁴ + 4 = (x² + 2x + 2)(x² − 2x + 2)
So (x⁴ + 4)/(x² − 2x + 2) = (x² + 2x + 2)(x² − 2x + 2)/(x² − 2x + 2)
Cancelling the common factor (x² − 2x + 2):
= x² + 2x + 2

Q: Q2 (vi). (z³ − 1)/(z² + z + 1)

Ans: Using a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²):
z³ − 1 = (z − 1)(z² + z + 1)
So (z³ − 1)/(z² + z + 1) = (z − 1)(z² + z + 1)/(z² + z + 1)
Cancelling the common factor (z² + z + 1):
= z − 1

mcqs.q: Which expression is in its lowest term?
mcqs.why: The numerator x + 1 and the denominator 2x − 1 share no common factor, so nothing can be cancelled. An expression is in its lowest term exactly when numerator and denominator have no common factor.

mcqs.q: Why is (3x² + 3)/(9x + 27) NOT in its lowest term?
options: Because 3x² + 3 = 3(x² + 1) and 9x + 27 = 9(x + 3) share the common factor 3
Because x² + 1 cannot be written down
Because 9 is a multiple of 3 in the denominator only
mcqs.why: Factorize both parts: numerator 3x² + 3 = 3(x² + 1) and denominator 9x + 27 = 9(x + 3). The factor 3 appears in both, so a common factor exists and the expression is not in its lowest term.

mcqs.q: (x² + 3x + 2)/(x + 2) is not in its lowest term because:
options: the denominator is a factor of nothing
x² + 3x + 2 = (x + 1)(x + 2), so (x + 2) is a common factor
mcqs.why: Factorize the numerator step by step: x² + 3x + 2 = x² + x + 2x + 2 = x(x + 1) + 2(x + 1) = (x + 1)(x + 2). The factor (x + 2) also appears in the denominator, so it can be cancelled.

mcqs.q: Reduce (x² − x − 6)/(x + 2) to lowest terms.
mcqs.why: Factorize: x² − x − 6 = x² − 3x + 2x − 6 = x(x − 3) + 2(x − 3) = (x − 3)(x + 2). Then (x − 3)(x + 2)/(x + 2), and cancelling the common factor (x + 2) leaves x − 3.

mcqs.q: Reduce (x³ + 1)/(x² − 1) to lowest terms.
mcqs.why: Use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²): x³ + 1 = (x + 1)(x² − x + 1). Use a² − b²: x² − 1 = (x + 1)(x − 1). Cancelling the common factor (x + 1) gives (x² − x + 1)/(x − 1).

mcqs.q: Reduce (x²y + xy)/(xy² − xy) to lowest terms.
mcqs.why: Factorize: numerator x²y + xy = xy(x + 1) and denominator xy² − xy = xy(y − 1). The quotient is xy(x + 1)/(xy(y − 1)), and cancelling the common factor xy gives (x + 1)/(y − 1).

mcqs.q: Reduce (x⁴ + 2x² + 1)/(x⁴ − 1) to lowest terms.
mcqs.why: Note x⁴ + 2x² + 1 = (x² + 1)² = (x² + 1)(x² + 1), and by a² − b², x⁴ − 1 = (x² + 1)(x² − 1). Cancelling the common factor (x² + 1) leaves (x² + 1)/(x² − 1).

mcqs.q: Reduce (x⁴ + 4)/(x² − 2x + 2) to lowest terms.
mcqs.why: Write x⁴ + 4 = (x² + 2)² − (2x)² and use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b): x⁴ + 4 = (x² + 2x + 2)(x² − 2x + 2). Dividing by (x² − 2x + 2) cancels that factor, leaving x² + 2x + 2.

mcqs.q: Reduce (z³ − 1)/(z² + z + 1) to lowest terms.
mcqs.why: Use a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) with a = z and b = 1: z³ − 1 = (z − 1)(z² + z + 1). Then (z − 1)(z² + z + 1)/(z² + z + 1), and cancelling (z² + z + 1) leaves z − 1.

mcqs.q: Which expression is in its lowest term?
mcqs.why: 4x² + 3 cannot be factorized and shares no factor with x + 3, so no cancellation is possible and the expression is already in its lowest term. Each other option has a visible common factor.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To add or subtract rational expressions, first take the L.C.M. of the denominators and rewrite each fraction over it.
  • 1/(y − 1) + 1/(y + 1) = 2y/(y² − 1), using (y − 1)(y + 1) = y² − 1.
  • 1/(a + b) + 1/(a − b) + 2a/(a² − b²) simplifies to 4a/(a² − b²).
  • To multiply rational expressions, factorize everything first and cancel the common factors before multiplying.
  • To divide by a rational expression, multiply by its reciprocal (invert the second expression), then factorize and cancel.
  • Useful factorizations here: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), and x² + 2xy + y² = (x + y)².

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Find the sum: (3x − 1)/(2x − 2) and 2/(x − 1)

Ans: (3x − 1)/(2x − 2) + 2/(x − 1)
2x − 2 = 2(x − 1), so the L.C.M. of the denominators is 2(x − 1).
= (3x − 1)/(2(x − 1)) + 4/(2(x − 1))
= (3x − 1 + 4)/(2(x − 1))
= (3x + 3)/(2x − 2)

Q: Q1 (ii). (2x + y)/(xy) and 3y/x

Ans: (2x + y)/(xy) + 3y/x
The L.C.M. of the denominators xy and x is xy.
= (2x + y)/(xy) + 3y²/(xy)
= (2x + y + 3y²)/(xy)
= (3y² + 2x + y)/(xy)

Q: Q1 (iii). 1/(y − 1) and 1/(y + 1)

Ans: 1/(y − 1) + 1/(y + 1)
The L.C.M. of the denominators is (y − 1)(y + 1) = y² − 1.
= ((y + 1) + (y − 1))/((y − 1)(y + 1))
= 2y/(y² − 1)

Q: Q1 (iv). 2y/(y² + 1) and 4y/(y² − 1)

Ans: 2y/(y² + 1) + 4y/(y² − 1)
The L.C.M. of the denominators is (y² + 1)(y² − 1) = y⁴ − 1.
= (2y(y² − 1) + 4y(y² + 1))/((y² + 1)(y² − 1))
= (2y³ − 2y + 4y³ + 4y)/(y⁴ − 1)
= (6y³ + 2y)/(y⁴ − 1)

Q: Q1 (v). (xy² + y)/(x + 3) and (x²y + x)/(x + 3)

Ans: The denominators are the same, so add the numerators:
= (xy² + y + x²y + x)/(x + 3)
Numerator = xy(x + y) + (x + y)
= (x + y)(xy + 1)
So the sum = (x + y)(xy + 1)/(x + 3)

Q: Q2 (i). Subtract the 1st expression from the 2nd: 15/(4y − 3), 16/(4y + 3)

Ans: 2nd − 1st = 16/(4y + 3) − 15/(4y − 3)
The L.C.M. of the denominators is (4y + 3)(4y − 3) = 16y² − 9.
= (16(4y − 3) − 15(4y + 3))/((4y + 3)(4y − 3))
= (64y − 48 − 60y − 45)/(16y² − 9)
= (4y − 93)/(16y² − 9)

Q: Q2 (ii). 1/(a + b), 1/(a − b)

Ans: 2nd − 1st = 1/(a − b) − 1/(a + b)
The L.C.M. of the denominators is (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b².
= ((a + b) − (a − b))/((a − b)(a + b))
= (a + b − a + b)/(a² − b²)
= 2b/(a² − b²)

Q: Q2 (iii). (x + y)/y, (x² − y²)/(xy)

Ans: 2nd − 1st = (x² − y²)/(xy) − (x + y)/y
The L.C.M. of the denominators is xy.
= (x² − y²)/(xy) − x(x + y)/(xy)
= (x² − y² − x² − xy)/(xy)
= (−y² − xy)/(xy)
= −y(y + x)/(xy)
= −(x + y)/x

Q: Q2 (iv). (2x + 1)/(x + 1), (2x − 1)/(x − 1)

Ans: 2nd − 1st = (2x − 1)/(x − 1) − (2x + 1)/(x + 1)
The L.C.M. of the denominators is (x − 1)(x + 1) = x² − 1.
= ((2x − 1)(x + 1) − (2x + 1)(x − 1))/((x − 1)(x + 1))
(2x − 1)(x + 1) = 2x² + 2x − x − 1 = 2x² + x − 1
(2x + 1)(x − 1) = 2x² − 2x + x − 1 = 2x² − x − 1
= ((2x² + x − 1) − (2x² − x − 1))/(x² − 1)
= 2x/(x² − 1)

Q: Q3 (i). Find the product: (49x² − 4y²)/(x² − 9) and (x − 3)/(7x − 2y)

Ans: Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
49x² − 4y² = (7x + 2y)(7x − 2y)
x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3)
Product = (7x + 2y)(7x − 2y)(x − 3)/((x + 3)(x − 3)(7x − 2y))
Cancelling the common factors (7x − 2y) and (x − 3):
= (7x + 2y)/(x + 3)

Q: Q3 (ii). (x³ − y³)/(x² + 2xy + y²) and (x + y)/(x² + xy + y²)

Ans: Using a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²):
x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²)
x² + 2xy + y² = (x + y)²
Product = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²)(x + y)/((x + y)²(x² + xy + y²))
Cancelling the common factors (x + y) and (x² + xy + y²):
= (x − y)/(x + y)

Q: Q3 (iii). (4x² + 12xy + 9y²)/(2x² + 5xy + 3y²) and (3x + 3)/(x² − 1)

Ans: Note: in the book the sign before 3y² in the first denominator is misprinted as "="; it is +.
4x² + 12xy + 9y² = (2x + 3y)²
2x² + 5xy + 3y² = 2x² + 2xy + 3xy + 3y²
= 2x(x + y) + 3y(x + y)
= (2x + 3y)(x + y)
x² − 1 = (x + 1)(x − 1)
Product = (2x + 3y)² × 3(x + 1)/((2x + 3y)(x + y)(x + 1)(x − 1))
Cancelling the common factors (2x + 3y) and (x + 1):
= 3(2x + 3y)/((x + y)(x − 1))

Q: Q3 (iv). (x³ + a³)/(x + a) and (x + a)/(x³ − a³)

Ans: Product = (x³ + a³)/(x + a) × (x + a)/(x³ − a³)
Cancelling the common factor (x + a):
= (x³ + a³)/(x³ − a³)

Q: Q4 (i). Divide: (2x² + 13x + 15)/(4x² − 1) by (2x² + 11x + 5)/(4x² − 1)

Ans: Division is changed into multiplication by inverting the second expression:
= (2x² + 13x + 15)/(4x² − 1) × (4x² − 1)/(2x² + 11x + 5)
Cancelling (4x² − 1):
= (2x² + 13x + 15)/(2x² + 11x + 5)
2x² + 13x + 15 = (2x + 3)(x + 5)
2x² + 11x + 5 = (2x + 1)(x + 5)
= (2x + 3)(x + 5)/((2x + 1)(x + 5))
Cancelling (x + 5):
= (2x + 3)/(2x + 1)

Q: Q4 (ii). a + 2/x² by (a + 2)/x²

Ans: a + 2/x² = (ax² + 2)/x²
= (ax² + 2)/x² ÷ (a + 2)/x²
= (ax² + 2)/x² × x²/(a + 2)
Cancelling x²:
= (ax² + 2)/(a + 2)

Q: Q4 (iii). (4 − x²)/(x² − 9) by (12 + 6x)/(x² − 6x + 9)

Ans: = (4 − x²)/(x² − 9) × (x² − 6x + 9)/(12 + 6x)
4 − x² = (2 − x)(2 + x)
x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3)
x² − 6x + 9 = (x − 3)²
12 + 6x = 6(2 + x)
= (2 − x)(2 + x)(x − 3)²/((x − 3)(x + 3) × 6(2 + x))
Cancelling the common factors (2 + x) and (x − 3):
= (2 − x)(x − 3)/(6(x + 3))

Q: Q4 (iv). (x⁸ − 1)/(4x² − 4) by (x⁴ − 1)/(x − 2)

Ans: = (x⁸ − 1)/(4x² − 4) × (x − 2)/(x⁴ − 1)
Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) twice:
x⁸ − 1 = (x⁴ − 1)(x⁴ + 1)
4x² − 4 = 4(x² − 1)
= (x⁴ − 1)(x⁴ + 1)(x − 2)/(4(x² − 1)(x⁴ − 1))
Cancelling the common factor (x⁴ − 1):
= (x⁴ + 1)(x − 2)/(4(x² − 1))

Q: Q5 (i). Simplify: 1/(a + b) + 1/(a − b) + 2a/(a² − b²)

Ans: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), so the L.C.M. of the denominators is a² − b².
= ((a − b) + (a + b) + 2a)/((a + b)(a − b))
= (a − b + a + b + 2a)/(a² − b²)
= 4a/(a² − b²)

Q: Q5 (ii). (x² − x − 20)/(x² − 25) × (x² − x − 2)/(x² + 2x − 8) ÷ (x + 1)/(x² + 25)

Ans: Change the division into multiplication by (x² + 25)/(x + 1), and factorize:
x² − x − 20 = (x − 5)(x + 4)
x² − 25 = (x − 5)(x + 5)
x² − x − 2 = (x − 2)(x + 1)
x² + 2x − 8 = (x + 4)(x − 2)
Expression = (x − 5)(x + 4)/((x − 5)(x + 5)) × (x − 2)(x + 1)/((x + 4)(x − 2)) × (x² + 25)/(x + 1)
Cancelling (x − 5), (x + 4), (x − 2) and (x + 1):
= (x² + 25)/(x + 5)

Q: Q5 (iii). (2x² + 9x + 9)/(3x² − 27) × (4x² + 8x + 3)/(x − 3) ÷ (2x + 3)²/((3x − 9)(x − 3))

Ans: Change the division into multiplication by ((3x − 9)(x − 3))/(2x + 3)², and factorize:
2x² + 9x + 9 = (2x + 3)(x + 3)
3x² − 27 = 3(x − 3)(x + 3)
4x² + 8x + 3 = (2x + 1)(2x + 3)
3x − 9 = 3(x − 3)
Expression = (2x + 3)(x + 3)/(3(x − 3)(x + 3)) × (2x + 1)(2x + 3)/(x − 3) × 3(x − 3)(x − 3)/(2x + 3)²
Cancelling 3, (x + 3), (x − 3)² and (2x + 3)²:
= 2x + 1

mcqs.why: Since 2x − 2 = 2(x − 1), the L.C.M. of the denominators is 2(x − 1). Rewrite the second fraction as 4/(2(x − 1)). Then add numerators: (3x − 1 + 4)/(2(x − 1)) = (3x + 3)/(2x − 2).

mcqs.q: (2x + y)/(xy) + 3y/x equals:
mcqs.why: The L.C.M. of the denominators xy and x is xy. Rewrite 3y/x as 3y²/(xy) by multiplying numerator and denominator by y. Then (2x + y + 3y²)/(xy) = (3y² + 2x + y)/(xy).

mcqs.q: 2y/(y² + 1) + 4y/(y² − 1) equals:
mcqs.why: The L.C.M. is (y² + 1)(y² − 1) = y⁴ − 1. Numerator: 2y(y² − 1) + 4y(y² + 1) = 2y³ − 2y + 4y³ + 4y = 6y³ + 2y. So the sum is (6y³ + 2y)/(y⁴ − 1).

mcqs.q: (xy² + y)/(x + 3) + (x²y + x)/(x + 3) equals:
mcqs.why: The denominators are already the same, so add numerators: xy² + y + x²y + x. Group: xy(x + y) + (x + y) = (x + y)(xy + 1). Hence the sum is (x + y)(xy + 1)/(x + 3).

mcqs.q: Subtracting 15/(4y − 3) from 16/(4y + 3) gives:
Subtracting 1/(a + b) from 1/(a − b) gives:
mcqs.why: 2nd − 1st = 1/(a − b) − 1/(a + b) with L.C.M. (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b². Numerator: (a + b) − (a − b) = a + b − a + b = 2b. So the difference is 2b/(a² − b²).

mcqs.q: Subtracting (x + y)/y from (x² − y²)/(xy) gives:
mcqs.why: 2nd − 1st = (x² − y²)/(xy) − (x + y)/y. With L.C.M. xy, rewrite the second fraction as x(x + y)/(xy). Numerator: x² − y² − x² − xy = −y² − xy = −y(y + x). So −y(x + y)/(xy) = −(x + y)/x.

mcqs.q: Subtracting (2x + 1)/(x + 1) from (2x − 1)/(x − 1) gives:
mcqs.why: With L.C.M. (x − 1)(x + 1) = x² − 1: (2x − 1)(x + 1) = 2x² + x − 1 and (2x + 1)(x − 1) = 2x² − x − 1. Subtracting: (2x² + x − 1) − (2x² − x − 1) = 2x. Result: 2x/(x² − 1).

mcqs.q: The product of (49x² − 4y²)/(x² − 9) and (x − 3)/(7x − 2y) is:
mcqs.why: Use a² − b²: 49x² − 4y² = (7x + 2y)(7x − 2y) and x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3). The product is (7x + 2y)(7x − 2y)(x − 3)/((x + 3)(x − 3)(7x − 2y)). Cancel (7x − 2y) and (x − 3): (7x + 2y)/(x + 3).

mcqs.q: The product of (x³ − y³)/(x² + 2xy + y²) and (x + y)/(x² + xy + y²) is:
mcqs.why: Use a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²): x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²), and x² + 2xy + y² = (x + y)². Product = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²)(x + y)/((x + y)²(x² + xy + y²)). Cancel (x + y) and (x² + xy + y²): (x − y)/(x + y).

mcqs.q: The product of (4x² + 12xy + 9y²)/(2x² + 5xy + 3y²) and (3x + 3)/(x² − 1) is:
(2x² + 13x + 15)/(4x² − 1) divided by (2x² + 11x + 5)/(4x² − 1) equals:
mcqs.why: Invert the divisor and multiply; the common (4x² − 1) cancels, giving (2x² + 13x + 15)/(2x² + 11x + 5). Factorize: 2x² + 13x + 15 = (2x + 3)(x + 5) and 2x² + 11x + 5 = (2x + 1)(x + 5). Cancel (x + 5): (2x + 3)/(2x + 1).

mcqs.q: (x⁸ − 1)/(4x² − 4) divided by (x⁴ − 1)/(x − 2) equals:
mcqs.why: Invert the divisor: (x⁸ − 1)/(4x² − 4) × (x − 2)/(x⁴ − 1). Use a² − b² twice: x⁸ − 1 = (x⁴ − 1)(x⁴ + 1), and 4x² − 4 = 4(x² − 1). Cancelling the common factor (x⁴ − 1) gives (x⁴ + 1)(x − 2)/(4(x² − 1)).

mcqs.q: 1/(a + b) + 1/(a − b) + 2a/(a² − b²) simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Since a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), the L.C.M. of the denominators is a² − b². The sum is ((a − b) + (a + b) + 2a)/(a² − b²) = (a − b + a + b + 2a)/(a² − b²) = 4a/(a² − b²).

lessons.title: Exercise 1.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The value of an expression is found by substituting the given values for the variables and then simplifying.
  • 5x + 3 at x = 1/3 is 14/3, and at x = −1 it is −2.
  • x³ + y³ + z³ at x = 3, y = 1, z = 4 is 27 + 1 + 64 = 92.
  • H = 2ab/(a + b) at a = 4, b = 2 gives H = 16/6 = 8/3.
  • For f(x) = x³ − 2x² + x − 1, f(−1/2) = −17/8; take care with signs when squaring and cubing negative fractions.
  • Even powers of a negative number are positive: (−2)⁴ = 16, which is used in x⁴/2 + y⁴/3 − z⁴/4 = 31 at x = 2, y = 3, z = −2.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. Find the values of 5x + 3 at x = 1/3 and x = −1.

Ans: Put x = 1/3 in 5x + 3:
= 5(1/3) + 3
= 5/3 + 3
= 14/3
Put x = −1 in 5x + 3:
= 5(−1) + 3
= −5 + 3
= −2

Q: Q2. Find the value of x³ + y³ + z³ at x = 3, y = 1 and z = 4.

Ans: Put x = 3, y = 1 and z = 4 in x³ + y³ + z³:
= (3)³ + (1)³ + (4)³
= 27 + 1 + 64
= 92

Q: Q3. Find the value of H = 2ab/(a + b) at a = 4, b = 2.

Ans: Put a = 4 and b = 2 in H = 2ab/(a + b):
H = 2(4)(2)/(4 + 2)
= 16/6
= 8/3

Q: Q4. f(x) = x³ − 2x² + x − 1. Find f(−1/2).

Ans: Put x = −1/2 in f(x) = x³ − 2x² + x − 1:
f(−1/2) = (−1/2)³ − 2(−1/2)² + (−1/2) − 1
= −1/8 − 2(1/4) − 1/2 − 1
= −1/8 − 1/2 − 1/2 − 1
= −17/8

Q: Q5. Find the value of the expression x⁴/2 + y⁴/3 − z⁴/4 at x = 2, y = 3 and z = −2.

Ans: Put x = 2, y = 3 and z = −2:
= (2)⁴/2 + (3)⁴/3 − (−2)⁴/4
= 16/2 + 81/3 − 16/4
= 8 + 27 − 4
= 31

Q: Q6. Find the value of x³ + 2xyz + z³ at x = 2, z = 3 and y = 4.

Ans: Put x = 2, y = 4 and z = 3 in x³ + 2xyz + z³:
= (2)³ + 2(2)(4)(3) + (3)³
= 8 + 48 + 27
= 83

Q: Q7. Compute the value of (xyz + 3xy²)/(x + y) at x = 1, y = 1 and z = 1.

Ans: Put x = 1, y = 1 and z = 1:
= ((1)(1)(1) + 3(1)(1)²)/(1 + 1)
= (1 + 3)/2
= 4/2
= 2

mcqs.q: The value of 5x + 3 at x = 1/3 is:
mcqs.why: Substitute x = 1/3 into 5x + 3: 5(1/3) + 3 = 5/3 + 3 = 5/3 + 9/3 = 14/3. Every step is shown: multiply first, then write 3 as 9/3 to add the fractions.

mcqs.q: The value of 5x + 3 at x = −1 is:
mcqs.why: Substitute x = −1 into 5x + 3: 5(−1) + 3 = −5 + 3 = −2. The product 5 × (−1) is negative, and adding 3 then gives −2.

mcqs.q: The value of x³ + y³ + z³ at x = 3, y = 1 and z = 4 is:
mcqs.why: Substitute the values: (3)³ + (1)³ + (4)³. Compute each cube: 27 + 1 + 64. Add step by step: 27 + 1 = 28, and 28 + 64 = 92.

mcqs.q: The value of H = 2ab/(a + b) at a = 4 and b = 2 is:
mcqs.why: Substitute a = 4 and b = 2: H = 2(4)(2)/(4 + 2). Numerator: 2 × 4 × 2 = 16. Denominator: 4 + 2 = 6. So H = 16/6, and dividing numerator and denominator by 2 gives 8/3.

mcqs.q: If f(x) = x³ − 2x² + x − 1, then f(−1/2) is:
The value of x⁴/2 + y⁴/3 − z⁴/4 at x = 2, y = 3 and z = −2 is:
mcqs.why: Substitute: (2)⁴/2 + (3)⁴/3 − (−2)⁴/4. Compute the powers: 16/2 + 81/3 − 16/4 (note (−2)⁴ = +16). Simplify each term: 8 + 27 − 4 = 31.

mcqs.q: The value of x³ + 2xyz + z³ at x = 2, y = 4 and z = 3 is:
mcqs.why: Substitute: (2)³ + 2(2)(4)(3) + (3)³. Compute each part: 8 + 48 + 27, where the middle term is 2 × 2 × 4 × 3 = 48. Add: 8 + 48 = 56, and 56 + 27 = 83.

mcqs.q: The value of (xyz + 3xy²)/(x + y) at x = 1, y = 1 and z = 1 is:
mcqs.why: Substitute x = 1, y = 1, z = 1: numerator = (1)(1)(1) + 3(1)(1)² = 1 + 3 = 4, and denominator = 1 + 1 = 2. So the value is 4/2 = 2.

mcqs.q: In evaluating x³ + y³ + z³ at x = 3, y = 1, z = 4, the term (4)³ equals:
mcqs.why: The cube of 4 means 4 × 4 × 4. Step by step: 4 × 4 = 16, and 16 × 4 = 64. This is the z³ term in the substitution (3)³ + (1)³ + (4)³ = 27 + 1 + 64.

mcqs.q: In evaluating x³ + 2xyz + z³ at x = 2, y = 4, z = 3, the middle term 2xyz equals:
mcqs.why: Substitute into the middle term only: 2xyz = 2 × (2) × (4) × (3). Multiply step by step: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 4 = 16, and 16 × 3 = 48. The full expression is then 8 + 48 + 27 = 83.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.5
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).
  • Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.
  • From Formula 1, a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2; for a + b = 8 and a − b = 2 this gives 34.
  • From Formula 2, ab = ((a + b)² − (a − b)²)/4; for a + b = 50 and a − b = 16 this gives 561.
  • (x + y)² + (x − y)² simplifies to 2(x² + y²) by Formula 1 with a = x and b = y.
  • (5x + 2y)² − (5x − 2y)² simplifies to 40xy by Formula 2 with a = 5x and b = 2y.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Simplify with the help of formulae: (x + y)² + (x − y)²

Ans: Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)
Put a = x and b = y:
(x + y)² + (x − y)² = 2(x² + y²)

Q: Q1 (ii). (2x² + 3y²)² + (2x² − 3y²)²

Ans: Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)
Put a = 2x² and b = 3y²:
= 2((2x²)² + (3y²)²)
= 2(4x⁴ + 9y⁴)
= 8x⁴ + 18y⁴

Q: Q1 (iii). (x + 4y²)² − (x − 4y²)²

Ans: Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
Put a = x and b = 4y²:
= 4(x)(4y²)
= 16xy²

Q: Q1 (iv). (3x + 9y²)² − (3x − 9y²)²

Ans: Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
Put a = 3x and b = 9y²:
= 4(3x)(9y²)
= 108xy²

Q: Q1 (v). (4x² + y)² + (4x² − y)²

Ans: Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)
Put a = 4x² and b = y:
= 2((4x²)² + y²)
= 2(16x⁴ + y²)
= 32x⁴ + 2y²

Q: Q1 (vi). (5x + 2y)² − (5x − 2y)²

Ans: Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
Put a = 5x and b = 2y:
= 4(5x)(2y)
= 40xy

Q: Q2 (i). Find the value of a² + b² when a + b = 2, a − b = 1.

Ans: Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)
So a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2
Put a + b = 2 and a − b = 1:
a² + b² = ((2)² + (1)²)/2
= (4 + 1)/2
= 5/2

Q: Q2 (ii). a + b = 8, a − b = 2.

Ans: Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)
So a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2
Put a + b = 8 and a − b = 2:
a² + b² = ((8)² + (2)²)/2
= (64 + 4)/2
= 68/2
= 34

Q: Q3 (i). Find the value of ab when a + b = 50, a − b = 16.

Ans: Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
So ab = ((a + b)² − (a − b)²)/4
Put a + b = 50 and a − b = 16:
ab = ((50)² − (16)²)/4
= (2500 − 256)/4
= 2244/4
= 561

Q: Q3 (ii). a + b = 60, a − b = 20.

Ans: Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
So ab = ((a + b)² − (a − b)²)/4
Put a + b = 60 and a − b = 20:
ab = ((60)² − (20)²)/4
= (3600 − 400)/4
= 3200/4
= 800

Q: Q3 (iii). a + b = 40, a − b = 12.

Ans: Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
So ab = ((a + b)² − (a − b)²)/4
Put a + b = 40 and a − b = 12:
ab = ((40)² − (12)²)/4
= (1600 − 144)/4
= 1456/4
= 364

Q: Q3 (iv). a + b = 6, a − b = 2.

Ans: Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
So ab = ((a + b)² − (a − b)²)/4
Put a + b = 6 and a − b = 2:
ab = ((6)² − (2)²)/4
= (36 − 4)/4
= 32/4
= 8

mcqs.q: (x + y)² + (x − y)² simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). Put a = x and b = y: (x + y)² + (x − y)² = 2(x² + y²). No expansion is needed once the formula is spotted.

mcqs.q: (2x² + 3y²)² + (2x² − 3y²)² simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 1 with a = 2x² and b = 3y²: the sum equals 2((2x²)² + (3y²)²). Compute the squares: (2x²)² = 4x⁴ and (3y²)² = 9y⁴. Then 2(4x⁴ + 9y⁴) = 8x⁴ + 18y⁴.

mcqs.q: (x + 4y²)² − (x − 4y²)² simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab. Put a = x and b = 4y²: the difference equals 4(x)(4y²). Multiply step by step: 4 × 4 = 16, so the result is 16xy².

mcqs.q: (3x + 9y²)² − (3x − 9y²)² simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 2 with a = 3x and b = 9y²: the difference equals 4(3x)(9y²). Multiply the numbers: 4 × 3 × 9 = 108, and the variables give x·y², so the result is 108xy².

mcqs.q: (4x² + y)² + (4x² − y)² simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 1 with a = 4x² and b = y: the sum equals 2((4x²)² + y²). Compute (4x²)² = 16x⁴. Then 2(16x⁴ + y²) = 32x⁴ + 2y².

mcqs.q: (5x + 2y)² − (5x − 2y)² simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 2 with a = 5x and b = 2y: the difference equals 4(5x)(2y). Multiply the numbers step by step: 4 × 5 × 2 = 40, and the variables give xy, so the result is 40xy.

mcqs.q: If a + b = 2 and a − b = 1, then a² + b² equals:
mcqs.why: From Formula 1, a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2. Substitute a + b = 2 and a − b = 1: ((2)² + (1)²)/2 = (4 + 1)/2 = 5/2.

mcqs.q: If a + b = 8 and a − b = 2, then a² + b² equals:
mcqs.why: From Formula 1, a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2. Substitute: ((8)² + (2)²)/2 = (64 + 4)/2 = 68/2 = 34.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.6
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca).
  • Rearranged: a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca).
  • Rearranged: ab + bc + ca = ((a + b + c)² − (a² + b² + c²))/2.
  • When a + b + c = 3 and ab + bc + ca = 2, then a² + b² + c² = 9 − 4 = 5.
  • Finding a + b + c from its square needs a square root, so the answer carries a ± sign, for example a + b + c = ±2√3 when (a + b + c)² = 12.
  • When a + b + c = 7 and a² + b² + c² = 67, then ab + bc + ca = (49 − 67)/2 = −9, a negative value.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Find the value of a² + b² + c² when ab + bc + ca = 2, a + b + c = 3.

Ans: Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
So a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca)
Put a + b + c = 3 and ab + bc + ca = 2:
= (3)² − 2(2)
= 9 − 4
= 5

Q: Q1 (ii). ab + bc + ca = 8, a + b + c = 4.

Ans: Formula 3: a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca)
Put a + b + c = 4 and ab + bc + ca = 8:
= (4)² − 2(8)
= 16 − 16
= 0

Q: Q1 (iii). ab + bc + ca = 5, a + b + c = 6.

Ans: Formula 3: a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca)
Put a + b + c = 6 and ab + bc + ca = 5:
= (6)² − 2(5)
= 36 − 10
= 26

Q: Q2 (i). Find the value of a + b + c when ab + bc + ca = 3, a² + b² + c² = 6.

Ans: Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
Put a² + b² + c² = 6 and ab + bc + ca = 3:
(a + b + c)² = 6 + 2(3)
= 6 + 6
= 12
Taking square root of both sides:
a + b + c = ±√12 = ±2√3

Q: Q2 (ii). ab + bc + ca = 5, a² + b² + c² = 2.

Ans: Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
Put a² + b² + c² = 2 and ab + bc + ca = 5:
(a + b + c)² = 2 + 2(5)
= 2 + 10
= 12
Taking square root of both sides:
a + b + c = ±√12 = ±2√3

Q: Q2 (iii). ab + bc + ca = 7, a² + b² + c² = 4.

Ans: Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
Put a² + b² + c² = 4 and ab + bc + ca = 7:
(a + b + c)² = 4 + 2(7)
= 4 + 14
= 18
Taking square root of both sides:
a + b + c = ±√18 = ±3√2

Q: Q3 (i). Find the value of ab + bc + ca when a + b + c = 6, a² + b² + c² = 2.

Ans: Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
So ab + bc + ca = ((a + b + c)² − (a² + b² + c²))/2
Put a + b + c = 6 and a² + b² + c² = 2:
= ((6)² − 2)/2
= (36 − 2)/2
= 34/2
= 17

Q: Q3 (ii). a + b + c = 9, a² + b² + c² = 13.

Ans: Formula 3: ab + bc + ca = ((a + b + c)² − (a² + b² + c²))/2
Put a + b + c = 9 and a² + b² + c² = 13:
= ((9)² − 13)/2
= (81 − 13)/2
= 68/2
= 34

Q: Q3 (iii). a + b + c = 7, a² + b² + c² = 67.

Ans: Formula 3: ab + bc + ca = ((a + b + c)² − (a² + b² + c²))/2
Put a + b + c = 7 and a² + b² + c² = 67:
= ((7)² − 67)/2
= (49 − 67)/2
= −18/2
= −9

mcqs.q: Formula 3 states that (a + b + c)² equals:
mcqs.why: Formula 3 is (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca). The cross terms ab, bc and ca each appear with coefficient 2, which is what all three rearrangements in this exercise are based on.

mcqs.q: If a + b + c = 3 and ab + bc + ca = 2, then a² + b² + c² equals:
mcqs.why: Rearrange Formula 3: a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca). Substitute the values: (3)² − 2(2) = 9 − 4 = 5.

mcqs.q: If a + b + c = 4 and ab + bc + ca = 8, then a² + b² + c² equals:
mcqs.why: Use a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca). Substitute a + b + c = 4 and ab + bc + ca = 8: (4)² − 2(8) = 16 − 16 = 0.

mcqs.q: If a + b + c = 6 and ab + bc + ca = 5, then a² + b² + c² equals:
mcqs.why: Use a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca). Substitute: (6)² − 2(5) = 36 − 10 = 26.

mcqs.q: If ab + bc + ca = 3 and a² + b² + c² = 6, then a + b + c equals:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca) = 6 + 2(3) = 6 + 6 = 12. Taking the square root of both sides: a + b + c = ±√12 = ±2√3, since √12 = √(4 × 3) = 2√3.

mcqs.q: If ab + bc + ca = 7 and a² + b² + c² = 4, then a + b + c equals:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 3: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca) = 4 + 2(7) = 4 + 14 = 18. Taking square roots: a + b + c = ±√18 = ±3√2, since √18 = √(9 × 2) = 3√2.

mcqs.q: If a + b + c = 6 and a² + b² + c² = 2, then ab + bc + ca equals:
mcqs.why: Rearrange Formula 3: ab + bc + ca = ((a + b + c)² − (a² + b² + c²))/2. Substitute: ((6)² − 2)/2 = (36 − 2)/2 = 34/2 = 17.

mcqs.q: If a + b + c = 9 and a² + b² + c² = 13, then ab + bc + ca equals:
If a + b + c = 7 and a² + b² + c² = 67, then ab + bc + ca equals:
mcqs.why: Use ab + bc + ca = ((a + b + c)² − (a² + b² + c²))/2. Substitute: ((7)² − 67)/2 = (49 − 67)/2 = −18/2 = −9. The result is negative because a² + b² + c² is larger than (a + b + c)².

mcqs.q: If ab + bc + ca = 5 and a² + b² + c² = 2, then (a + b + c)² equals:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 3 directly: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca). Substitute the values: 2 + 2(5) = 2 + 10 = 12. (Hence a + b + c = ±√12 = ±2√3.)

lessons.title: Exercise 1.7
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Formula 4: (a + b)³ = a³ + 3ab(a + b) + b³, which expands to a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³.
  • Formula 5: (a − b)³ = a³ − 3ab(a − b) − b³.
  • Formula 6: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab); Formula 7: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab).
  • From Formula 4, a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b); for a + b = 6 and ab = 4 this gives 216 − 72 = 144.
  • From Formula 5, x³ − y³ = (x − y)³ + 3xy(x − y); for x − y = 2 and xy = 12 this gives 8 + 72 = 80.
  • In a continued product, pair (x + 2y) with (x² − 2xy + 4y²) to get x³ + 8y³, and (x − 2y) with (x² + 2xy + 4y²) to get x³ − 8y³; the product is then x⁶ − 64y⁶ by a² − b².
  • To use Formulas 6 and 7 when a² + b² is not given, first find it from Formula 1: a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Expand with the help of formulas: (x + y)³

Ans: Formula 4: (a + b)³ = a³ + 3ab(a + b) + b³
Put a = x and b = y:
(x + y)³ = x³ + 3xy(x + y) + y³
= x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³

Q: Q1 (ii). (2x − 3y)³

Ans: Formula 5: (a − b)³ = a³ − 3ab(a − b) − b³
Put a = 2x and b = 3y:
(2x − 3y)³ = (2x)³ − 3(2x)(3y)(2x − 3y) − (3y)³
= 8x³ − 18xy(2x − 3y) − 27y³
= 8x³ − 36x²y + 54xy² − 27y³

Q: Q1 (iii). (1/x + (2/3)y)³

Ans: Formula 4: (a + b)³ = a³ + 3ab(a + b) + b³
Put a = 1/x and b = (2/3)y:
= (1/x)³ + 3(1/x)((2/3)y)(1/x + (2/3)y) + ((2/3)y)³
= 1/x³ + (2y/x)(1/x + (2/3)y) + 8y³/27
= 1/x³ + 2y/x² + 4y²/(3x) + 8y³/27

Q: Q2 (i). Reduce to the form (x ± y)³: x³ + 6xy(x + 2y) + 8y³

Ans: First expand the middle term:
x³ + 6xy(x + 2y) + 8y³ = x³ + 6x²y + 12xy² + 8y³
Compare with (x + 2y)³ = x³ + 3x²(2y) + 3x(2y)² + (2y)³
= x³ + 6x²y + 12xy² + 8y³
Both are equal, so:
x³ + 6xy(x + 2y) + 8y³ = (x + 2y)³

Q: Q2 (ii). x³ − 6x²y − 12xy² − 8y³ (as printed)

Ans: Note: the book prints the third term as −12xy², but in the cube of (x − 2y) it is +12xy²; the printed sign is a misprint.
(x − 2y)³ = x³ − 3x²(2y) + 3x(2y)² − (2y)³
= x³ − 6x²y + 12xy² − 8y³
So, with the corrected sign:
x³ − 6x²y + 12xy² − 8y³ = (x − 2y)³

Q: Q3. Find the value of a³ + b³ when a + b = 6 and ab = 4.

Ans: From Formula 4: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)
So a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b)
Put a + b = 6 and ab = 4:
a³ + b³ = (6)³ − 3(4)(6)
= 216 − 72
= 144

Q: Q4. Evaluate x³ − y³ when x − y = 2 and xy = 12.

Ans: From Formula 5: (x − y)³ = x³ − y³ − 3xy(x − y)
So x³ − y³ = (x − y)³ + 3xy(x − y)
Put x − y = 2 and xy = 12:
x³ − y³ = (2)³ + 3(12)(2)
= 8 + 72
= 80

Q: Q5 (i). Find the continued product: (x + 2y)(x − 2y)(x² + 4y² + 2xy)(x² + 4y² − 2xy)

Ans: Pair the factors so that Formulas 6 and 7 apply:
(x + 2y)(x² − 2xy + 4y²) = x³ + (2y)³ = x³ + 8y³
(x − 2y)(x² + 2xy + 4y²) = x³ − (2y)³ = x³ − 8y³
Continued product = (x³ + 8y³)(x³ − 8y³)
Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
= (x³)² − (8y³)²
= x⁶ − 64y⁶

Q: Q5 (ii). (2a + 3b)(2a − 3b)(4a² + 6ab + 9b²)(4a² − 6ab + 9b²)

Ans: Pair the factors so that Formulas 6 and 7 apply:
(2a + 3b)(4a² − 6ab + 9b²) = (2a)³ + (3b)³ = 8a³ + 27b³
(2a − 3b)(4a² + 6ab + 9b²) = (2a)³ − (3b)³ = 8a³ − 27b³
Continued product = (8a³ + 27b³)(8a³ − 27b³)
Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
= (8a³)² − (27b³)²
= 64a⁶ − 729b⁶

Q: Q6 (i). Find the value of a³ + b³ when a + b = 3, a − b = 5, ab = 4.

Ans: Formula 6: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab)
First find a² + b² by Formula 1:
a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2 = ((3)² + (5)²)/2 = (9 + 25)/2 = 17
Then a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab)
= 3 × (17 − 4)
= 3 × 13
= 39

Q: Q6 (ii). a + b = 2, a − b = 8, ab = 16.

Ans: Formula 6: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab)
First find a² + b² by Formula 1:
a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2 = ((2)² + (8)²)/2 = (4 + 64)/2 = 34
Then a³ + b³ = 2 × (34 − 16)
= 2 × 18
= 36

Q: Q6 (iii). a + b = 1, a − b = 4, ab = 12.

Ans: Formula 6: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab)
First find a² + b² by Formula 1:
a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2 = ((1)² + (4)²)/2 = (1 + 16)/2 = 17/2
Then a³ + b³ = 1 × (17/2 − 12)
= 17/2 − 24/2
= −7/2

Q: Q7 (i). Find the value of a³ − b³ when a + b = 7, a − b = 9, ab = 15.

Ans: Formula 7: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab)
First find a² + b² by Formula 1:
a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2 = ((7)² + (9)²)/2 = (49 + 81)/2 = 65
Then a³ − b³ = 9 × (65 + 15)
= 9 × 80
= 720

Q: Q7 (ii). a + b = 6, a − b = 10, ab = 3.

Ans: Formula 7: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab)
First find a² + b² by Formula 1:
a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2 = ((6)² + (10)²)/2 = (36 + 100)/2 = 68
Then a³ − b³ = 10 × (68 + 3)
= 10 × 71
= 710

Q: Q7 (iii). a + b = 1, a − b = 1, ab = 3.

Ans: Formula 7: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab)
First find a² + b² by Formula 1:
a² + b² = ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2 = ((1)² + (1)²)/2 = 2/2 = 1
Then a³ − b³ = 1 × (1 + 3)
= 4

mcqs.q: (x + y)³ expands to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 4: (a + b)³ = a³ + 3ab(a + b) + b³ with a = x, b = y: (x + y)³ = x³ + 3xy(x + y) + y³. Now expand the middle term: 3xy(x + y) = 3x²y + 3xy², giving x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³.

mcqs.q: (2x − 3y)³ expands to:
mcqs.why: Use Formula 5: (a − b)³ = a³ − 3ab(a − b) − b³ with a = 2x, b = 3y: (2x)³ − 3(2x)(3y)(2x − 3y) − (3y)³ = 8x³ − 18xy(2x − 3y) − 27y³. Expand 18xy(2x − 3y) = 36x²y − 54xy², so the result is 8x³ − 36x²y + 54xy² − 27y³.

mcqs.q: (1/x + (2/3)y)³ expands to:
x³ + 6xy(x + 2y) + 8y³ reduces to the cube:
mcqs.why: First expand the middle term: 6xy(x + 2y) = 6x²y + 12xy², so the expression is x³ + 6x²y + 12xy² + 8y³. Compare with (x + 2y)³ = x³ + 3x²(2y) + 3x(2y)² + (2y)³ = x³ + 6x²y + 12xy² + 8y³. They match, so it equals (x + 2y)³.

mcqs.q: The corrected form x³ − 6x²y + 12xy² − 8y³ equals:
mcqs.why: Expand (x − 2y)³ term by term: x³ − 3x²(2y) + 3x(2y)² − (2y)³ = x³ − 6x²y + 12xy² − 8y³, which matches. Note: the book misprints the third term of this question as −12xy²; in the cube of (x − 2y) it must be +12xy², so the corrected sign is used here.

mcqs.q: If a + b = 6 and ab = 4, then a³ + b³ equals:
mcqs.why: From Formula 4, a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b). Substitute a + b = 6 and ab = 4: (6)³ − 3(4)(6) = 216 − 72 = 144.

mcqs.q: If x − y = 2 and xy = 12, then x³ − y³ equals:
mcqs.why: From Formula 5, x³ − y³ = (x − y)³ + 3xy(x − y). Substitute x − y = 2 and xy = 12: (2)³ + 3(12)(2) = 8 + 72 = 80.

mcqs.q: The continued product (x + 2y)(x − 2y)(x² + 4y² + 2xy)(x² + 4y² − 2xy) equals:
mcqs.why: Pair the factors for Formulas 6 and 7: (x + 2y)(x² − 2xy + 4y²) = x³ + (2y)³ = x³ + 8y³, and (x − 2y)(x² + 2xy + 4y²) = x³ − (2y)³ = x³ − 8y³. Then by a² − b²: (x³ + 8y³)(x³ − 8y³) = (x³)² − (8y³)² = x⁶ − 64y⁶.

mcqs.q: If a + b = 3, a − b = 5 and ab = 4, then a³ + b³ equals:
mcqs.why: First find a² + b² by Formula 1: ((a + b)² + (a − b)²)/2 = ((3)² + (5)²)/2 = (9 + 25)/2 = 17. Then Formula 6: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab) = 3 × (17 − 4) = 3 × 13 = 39.

mcqs.q: If a + b = 7, a − b = 9 and ab = 15, then a³ − b³ equals:
mcqs.why: First find a² + b² by Formula 1: ((7)² + (9)²)/2 = (49 + 81)/2 = 65. Then Formula 7: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab) = 9 × (65 + 15) = 9 × 80 = 720.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.8
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A surd is a root that cannot be removed to give a rational number, such as √2.
  • √4 = 2, √16 = 4 and √(9/4) = 3/2 are rational numbers, so they are not surds.
  • 3√2 is a mixed surd: a rational factor 3 multiplied by the surd √2.
  • Expressions such as 2 + √3, 2 − √3 and 1/√5 are surds because they contain the surds √3 or √5.
  • A second order surd has root order 2, for example √3, √7 and 2^(1/2) = √2; cube roots and fourth roots are not second order.
  • To rationalize 1/(denominator), multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator and use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
  • 1/(√3 − 1) rationalizes to (√3 + 1)/2, and 1/(√5 − √3) rationalizes to (√5 + √3)/2.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Which of the following numbers are surds? 3

Ans: 3 is a rational number; it has no root that cannot be removed.
Not a surd.

Q: Q1 (ii). √4

Ans: √4 = 2, which is a rational number.
So √4 is not a surd.

Q: Q1 (iii). √2

Ans: √2 cannot be written as a fraction of two integers.
So √2 is a surd.

Q: Q1 (iv). 3√2

Ans: 3√2 contains the surd √2 with rational factor 3.
So 3√2 is a (mixed) surd.

Q: Q1 (v). √16

Ans: √16 = 4, which is a rational number.
So √16 is not a surd.

Q: Q1 (vi). √(9/4)

Ans: √(9/4) = 3/2, which is a rational number.
So √(9/4) is not a surd.

Q: Q1 (vii). 1/√5

Ans: 1/√5 contains the surd √5 (its rationalized form is √5/5).
So 1/√5 is a surd.

Q: Q1 (viii). 2 + √3

Ans: 2 + √3 contains the surd √3.
So 2 + √3 is a surd.

Q: Q1 (ix). 2 − √3

Ans: 2 − √3 contains the surd √3.
So 2 − √3 is a surd.

Q: Q1 (x). √(17/4)

Ans: √(17/4) = √17/2, and √17 cannot be written as a fraction of two integers.
So √(17/4) is a surd.

Q: Q2 (i). Separate the second order surds: √3

Ans: √3 = 3^(1/2); the order of the root is 2.
Second order surd.

Q: Q2 (ii). Cube root of 3

Ans: The root here is a cube root, of order 3.
Not a second order surd.

Q: Q2 (iii). 2^(1/2)

Ans: 2^(1/2) = √2; the order of the root is 2.
Second order surd.

Q: Q2 (iv). Fourth root of 5

Ans: The root here is a fourth root, of order 4.
Not a second order surd.

Q: Q2 (v). √7

Ans: √7 = 7^(1/2); the order of the root is 2.
Second order surd.

Q: Q3 (i). Rationalize: 1/(√2 + 3)

Ans: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (3 − √2).
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
1/(√2 + 3) = (3 − √2)/((3 + √2)(3 − √2))
= (3 − √2)/(9 − 2)
= (3 − √2)/7

Q: Q3 (ii). 1/(√3 − 1)

Ans: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√3 + 1).
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
1/(√3 − 1) = (√3 + 1)/((√3 − 1)(√3 + 1))
= (√3 + 1)/(3 − 1)
= (√3 + 1)/2

Q: Q3 (iii). 1/(2√3 − 1)

Ans: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (2√3 + 1).
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
1/(2√3 − 1) = (2√3 + 1)/((2√3 − 1)(2√3 + 1))
= (2√3 + 1)/((2√3)² − 1²)
= (2√3 + 1)/(12 − 1)
= (2√3 + 1)/11

Q: Q3 (iv). 1/(√5 − √3)

Ans: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√5 + √3).
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
1/(√5 − √3) = (√5 + √3)/((√5 − √3)(√5 + √3))
= (√5 + √3)/(5 − 3)
= (√5 + √3)/2

Q: Q3 (v). 1/(√7 + √3)

Ans: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√7 − √3).
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
1/(√7 + √3) = (√7 − √3)/((√7 + √3)(√7 − √3))
= (√7 − √3)/(7 − 3)
= (√7 − √3)/4

mcqs.q: Which number is a surd?
mcqs.why: √2 cannot be written as a fraction of two integers and its root cannot be removed, so it is a surd. The others are rational: 3 is rational, √4 = 2 and √16 = 4.

mcqs.q: Why is √4 NOT a surd?
options: Because √4 = 2, which is a rational number
Because 4 is a perfect square greater than 1
mcqs.why: A surd must be a root that cannot be removed to leave a rational number. Here the root can be removed completely: √4 = 2, and 2 is rational, so √4 is not a surd.

mcqs.q: Which number is NOT a surd?
mcqs.why: The plain number 3 is a rational number and it has no root in it at all, so it is not a surd. Each other option contains a root that cannot be removed: √2, the √2 inside 3√2, and the √5 inside 1/√5.

mcqs.q: 3√2 is best described as:
options: not a surd, because 3 is rational
a mixed surd, containing the surd √2 with rational factor 3
a second order surd only if 3 is removed
mcqs.why: 3√2 is the rational number 3 multiplied by the surd √2. A rational factor times a surd is called a mixed surd, and it is still a surd because the root √2 cannot be removed.

mcqs.q: Why is √(9/4) NOT a surd?
options: Because √(9/4) = 3/2, which is a rational number
Because the root is over a fraction
Because 9 is a perfect square only
mcqs.why: Take the root of numerator and denominator separately: √(9/4) = √9/√4 = 3/2. Since 3/2 is a fraction of two integers, it is rational, and a rational number is not a surd.

mcqs.q: Which expression is a surd?
mcqs.why: 1/√5 contains √5, whose root cannot be removed (its rationalized form is √5/5, still containing √5), so it is a surd. The others simplify to the rational numbers 4, 3/2 and 2 respectively.

mcqs.q: Which expression is a surd?
mcqs.why: 2 + √3 contains the term √3, which cannot be written as a fraction of two integers, so the whole expression is a surd. The other options are the rational numbers 4, 3 and 3/2.

mcqs.q: Why is √(17/4) a surd?
options: Because √(17/4) = √17/2 and √17 cannot be written as a fraction of two integers
mcqs.why: Simplify first: √(17/4) = √17/√4 = √17/2. The factor √17 remains, and √17 is irrational — it cannot be written as a fraction of two integers — so √(17/4) is a surd.

mcqs.q: Which is a second order surd?
mcqs.why: √3 = 3^(1/2), so the order of its root is 2, making it a second order surd. A cube root has order 3 and a fourth root has order 4, so neither of those is second order.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a second order surd?
mcqs.why: The cube root of 3 is a root of order 3, not order 2, so it is not a second order surd. The others all have order 2: √7 = 7^(1/2), 2^(1/2) = √2 and √3 = 3^(1/2).

mcqs.q: 2^(1/2) is a second order surd because:
options: 2^(1/2) = √2, and the order of the root is 2
mcqs.why: The fractional exponent 1/2 means a square root: 2^(1/2) = √2. The order of a root is the denominator of that exponent, namely 2, so 2^(1/2) is a second order surd.

mcqs.q: The fourth root of 5 is not a second order surd because:
options: it cannot be a surd at all
mcqs.why: The order of a root is given by the root index. A fourth root has index 4, so its order is 4. Only roots of order 2 (square roots) count as second order surds, so the fourth root of 5 is excluded.

mcqs.q: Rationalizing 1/(√2 + 3) gives:
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (3 − √2). Using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b): (3 + √2)(3 − √2) = 9 − 2 = 7. So 1/(√2 + 3) = (3 − √2)/7, and the denominator is now rational.

mcqs.q: Rationalizing 1/(√3 − 1) gives:
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√3 + 1). Using a² − b²: (√3 − 1)(√3 + 1) = 3 − 1 = 2. So 1/(√3 − 1) = (√3 + 1)/2, with a rational denominator.

mcqs.q: Rationalizing 1/(√5 − √3) gives:
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√5 + √3). Using a² − b²: (√5 − √3)(√5 + √3) = 5 − 3 = 2. So 1/(√5 − √3) = (√5 + √3)/2, with a rational denominator.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • x² + 3x + 5 is a polynomial, and x/(x² + 1) is a rational expression.
  • (x − 1)/(x² − 1) is NOT in its lowest term, because x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1) gives the common factor (x − 1).
  • 1/2 IS a rational expression: the statement '1/2 is not a rational expression' is false.
  • In p(x)/q(x), q(x) must NOT be zero; the statement that q(x) must be zero is false.
  • The degree of x³ − 4x² + 3 is 3, the highest power of x.
  • (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) and (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.
  • a³ + b³ + 3a²b + 3ab² = (a + b)³, and (a − b)³ = a³ − 3ab(a − b) − b³.
  • Rationalization is the process in which surds appear in the numerator only; the rationalized form of 1/(√2 − 1) is √2 + 1.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). x² + 3x + 5 is a polynomial.

Ans: True

Q: Q1 (ii). x/(x² + 1) is a rational expression.

Ans: True

Q: Q1 (iii). (x − 1)/(x² − 1) is in the lowest term.

Ans: False

Q: Q1 (iv). 1/2 is not a rational expression.

Ans: False

Q: Q1 (v). In p(x)/q(x), q(x) must be zero.

Ans: False

Q: Q2 (i). Choose the correct option: The degree of x³ − 4x² + 3 is:

Options: (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 1 (d) 4

Correct answer: 3

Q: Q2 (ii). (a + b)² + (a − b)² =

Options: (a) 3(a² + b²) (b) 2(a² + b²) (c) (a² + b²) (d) 4ab

Correct answer: 2(a² + b²)

Q: Q2 (iii). (a + b)² − (a − b)² =

Options: (a) ab (b) 4ab (c) 2ab (d) −4ab

Correct answer: 4ab

Q: Q2 (iv). a³ + b³ + 3a²b + 3ab² =

Options: (a) (a − b)³ (b) (a + b)³ (c) a³ + b³ (d) a³

Correct answer: (a + b)³

Q: Q3 (i). The rationalized form of 1/(√2 − 1) is

Ans: √2 + 1

Q: Q3 (ii). The process in which surds appear in numerator only is called

Ans: Rationalization

Q: Q3 (iii). (a − b)³ =

Ans: a³ − 3ab(a − b) − b³

Q: Q3 (iv). (√5)³ − (√3)³ =

Ans: 5√5 − 3√3

mcqs.q: The degree of x³ − 4x² + 3 is:
mcqs.why: The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable in it. The powers of x here are 3, 2 and 0 (for the constant 3), and the highest is 3, so the degree is 3. This is the book's own MCQ and its keyed answer.

mcqs.q: (a + b)² + (a − b)² =
mcqs.why: This is Formula 1: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). Expanding to check: (a² + 2ab + b²) + (a² − 2ab + b²) = 2a² + 2b² = 2(a² + b²), because the +2ab and −2ab cancel.

mcqs.q: (a + b)² − (a − b)² =
mcqs.why: This is Formula 2: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab. Expanding to check: (a² + 2ab + b²) − (a² − 2ab + b²) = a² + 2ab + b² − a² + 2ab − b² = 4ab.

mcqs.q: a³ + b³ + 3a²b + 3ab² =
mcqs.why: Compare with Formula 4: (a + b)³ = a³ + 3ab(a + b) + b³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³. The given expression is exactly these four terms rearranged, so it equals (a + b)³.

mcqs.q: The rationalized form of 1/(√2 − 1) is:
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√2 + 1). Using a² − b²: (√2 − 1)(√2 + 1) = 2 − 1 = 1. So 1/(√2 − 1) = (√2 + 1)/1 = √2 + 1, with the surd now in the numerator only.

mcqs.q: The process in which surds appear in the numerator only is called:
mcqs.why: Rationalization means removing surds from the denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by a conjugate, so that any surd that remains appears in the numerator only. For example, 1/(√2 − 1) rationalizes to √2 + 1.

mcqs.q: (a − b)³ =
mcqs.why: This is Formula 5: (a − b)³ = a³ − 3ab(a − b) − b³. Expanding the middle term gives a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³, the standard cube of a difference, with alternating signs.
Compute each cube using (√n)³ = (√n)² × √n = n√n. So (√5)³ = 5√5 and (√3)³ = 3√3. Subtracting: 5√5 − 3√3.

mcqs.q: Which statement about (x − 1)/(x² − 1) is correct?
options: It is in its lowest term
It is not in its lowest term, because (x − 1) is a common factor
It is not a rational expression
It is in its lowest term because x² − 1 cannot be factorized
mcqs.why: Factorize the denominator using a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b): x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1). The factor (x − 1) is common to numerator and denominator, so the expression can be reduced to 1/(x + 1) and is not in its lowest term. The book's true/false key agrees: the statement that it is in the lowest term is False.

mcqs.q: In the rational expression p(x)/q(x), the correct condition on q(x) is:
options: q(x) may be any polynomial, including zero
mcqs.why: Division by zero is not allowed, so a rational expression p(x)/q(x) is defined only when q(x) is not zero. The book's true/false statement 'q(x) must be zero' is keyed False for exactly this reason.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Factorization by taking out a common factor: divide every term by the highest common factor and write it outside brackets.
  • For 2x − 8y the common factor is 2, giving 2(x − 4y).
  • For powers, the common factor uses the lowest power of each variable, e.g. 3x³ + 6x² = 3x²(x + 2).
  • 4x³y³ − x²y² = x²y²(4xy − 1) because x²y² divides both terms.
  • 28x²y⁴ − 35xy³ + 42x⁴y = 7xy(4xy³ − 5y² + 6x³); the common factor is 7xy.
  • 45x¹⁰y⁴ − 63x⁶y⁷ + 72x³y³ = 9x³y³(5x⁷y − 7x³y⁴ + 8).
  • Always check by expanding the brackets to recover the original expression.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Factorize: 2x − 8y

Ans: Take out the common factor 2:
2x − 8y = 2(x − 4y)

Q: 2. 3x³ + 6x²

Ans: Take out the common factor 3x²:
3x³ + 6x² = 3x²(x + 2)

Q: 3. 4x³y³ − x²y²

Ans: Take out the common factor x²y²:
4x³y³ − x²y² = x²y²(4xy − 1)

Q: 4. 2x + 2y − 4z

Ans: Take out the common factor 2:
2x + 2y − 4z = 2(x + y − 2z)

Q: 5. 16x⁴ − 4x³ + 2x²

Ans: Take out the common factor 2x²:
16x⁴ − 4x³ + 2x² = 2x²(8x² − 2x + 1)

Q: 6. 28x²y⁴ − 35xy³ + 42x⁴y

Ans: Take out the common factor 7xy:
28x²y⁴ − 35xy³ + 42x⁴y = 7xy(4xy³ − 5y² + 6x³)

Q: 7. 7abc − 14a²b²c²

Ans: Take out the common factor 7abc:
7abc − 14a²b²c² = 7abc(1 − 2abc)

Q: 8. 16x + 32xy²

Ans: Take out the common factor 16x:
16x + 32xy² = 16x(1 + 2y²)

Q: 9. 4x² + 8a²x² − 4a³x

Ans: Take out the common factor 4x:
4x² + 8a²x² − 4a³x = 4x(x + 2a²x − a³)

Q: 10. 45x¹⁰y⁴ − 63x⁶y⁷ + 72x³y³

Ans: Take out the common factor 9x³y³:
45x¹⁰y⁴ − 63x⁶y⁷ + 72x³y³ = 9x³y³(5x⁷y − 7x³y⁴ + 8)

mcqs.q: Factorize 2x − 8y.
mcqs.why: The highest common factor of 2x and 8y is 2. Step 1: 2x ÷ 2 = x. Step 2: −8y ÷ 2 = −4y. Step 3: write 2 outside brackets: 2x − 8y = 2(x − 4y).

mcqs.q: Factorize 3x³ + 6x².
mcqs.why: The common factor is 3x², the lowest power of x times 3. Step 1: 3x³ ÷ 3x² = x. Step 2: 6x² ÷ 3x² = 2. Step 3: 3x³ + 6x² = 3x²(x + 2).

mcqs.q: Factorize 4x³y³ − x²y².
mcqs.why: The common factor is x²y². Step 1: 4x³y³ ÷ x²y² = 4xy. Step 2: −x²y² ÷ x²y² = −1. Step 3: factorize as x²y²(4xy − 1), which expands back to the original.

mcqs.q: Factorize 2x + 2y − 4z.
mcqs.why: The common factor of all three terms is 2. Step 1: 2x ÷ 2 = x and 2y ÷ 2 = y. Step 2: −4z ÷ 2 = −2z. Step 3: 2x + 2y − 4z = 2(x + y − 2z).

mcqs.q: Factorize 16x⁴ − 4x³ + 2x².
mcqs.why: The common factor is 2x². Step 1: 16x⁴ ÷ 2x² = 8x². Step 2: −4x³ ÷ 2x² = −2x. Step 3: 2x² ÷ 2x² = 1. Hence 2x²(8x² − 2x + 1).

mcqs.q: Factorize 28x²y⁴ − 35xy³ + 42x⁴y.
mcqs.why: The common factor is 7xy. Step 1: 28x²y⁴ ÷ 7xy = 4xy³. Step 2: −35xy³ ÷ 7xy = −5y². Step 3: 42x⁴y ÷ 7xy = 6x³. So the result is 7xy(4xy³ − 5y² + 6x³).

mcqs.q: Factorize 7abc − 14a²b²c².
mcqs.why: The common factor is 7abc. Step 1: 7abc ÷ 7abc = 1. Step 2: −14a²b²c² ÷ 7abc = −2abc. Step 3: write the factorization as 7abc(1 − 2abc).

mcqs.q: Factorize 16x + 32xy².
mcqs.why: The common factor is 16x. Step 1: 16x ÷ 16x = 1. Step 2: 32xy² ÷ 16x = 2y². Step 3: 16x + 32xy² = 16x(1 + 2y²). Expanding checks the answer.

mcqs.q: Factorize 4x² + 8a²x² − 4a³x.
mcqs.why: The common factor is 4x. Step 1: 4x² ÷ 4x = x. Step 2: 8a²x² ÷ 4x = 2a²x. Step 3: −4a³x ÷ 4x = −a³. Hence 4x(x + 2a²x − a³).

mcqs.q: Factorize 45x¹⁰y⁴ − 63x⁶y⁷ + 72x³y³.
mcqs.why: The common factor is 9x³y³. Step 1: 45x¹⁰y⁴ ÷ 9x³y³ = 5x⁷y. Step 2: −63x⁶y⁷ ÷ 9x³y³ = −7x³y⁴. Step 3: 72x³y³ ÷ 9x³y³ = 8. Result: 9x³y³(5x⁷y − 7x³y⁴ + 8).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Factorization by grouping: group terms in pairs, factorize each pair, then take out the common binomial factor.
  • x² + xy + xz + yz = x(x + y) + z(x + y) = (x + y)(x + z).
  • ax − a − x + 1 = a(x − 1) − 1(x − 1) = (x − 1)(a − 1); watch signs when grouping with a minus.
  • 3x³ − 2x² + 18x − 12 = x²(3x − 2) + 6(3x − 2) = (3x − 2)(x² + 6).
  • With six terms, group to create the same factor, e.g. (x − y) in x² − xy + xz + 3x − 3y − yz = (x − y)(x + z + 3).
  • 2y⁵ + 3y⁴ + 2y³ + 3y² + 6y + 9 = (2y + 3)(y⁴ + y² + 3) by grouping in three pairs.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Factorize: x² + xy + xz + yz

Ans: Group the terms in pairs and take out the common factor of each pair:
x² + xy + xz + yz = (x² + xy) + (xz + yz)
= x(x + y) + z(x + y)
Take out the common factor (x + y):
= (x + y)(x + z)

Q: 2. a² + 2a + ab + 2b

Ans: a² + 2a + ab + 2b = (a² + 2a) + (ab + 2b)
= a(a + 2) + b(a + 2)
Take out the common factor (a + 2):
= (a + 2)(a + b)

Q: 3. a² − 2b³ − 2ab² + ab

Ans: a² − 2b³ − 2ab² + ab = (a² + ab) − (2ab² + 2b³)
= a(a + b) − 2b²(a + b)
Take out the common factor (a + b):
= (a + b)(a − 2b²)

Q: 4. ax − a − x + 1

Ans: ax − a − x + 1 = (ax − a) − (x − 1)
= a(x − 1) − 1(x − 1)
Take out the common factor (x − 1):
= (x − 1)(a − 1)

Q: 5. 3x³ − 2x² + 18x − 12

Ans: 3x³ − 2x² + 18x − 12 = (3x³ − 2x²) + (18x − 12)
= x²(3x − 2) + 6(3x − 2)
Take out the common factor (3x − 2):
= (3x − 2)(x² + 6)

Q: 6. 3x + y + 3ax + ay + 3bx + by

Ans: Arrange the terms so that (1 + a + b) becomes common:
3x + y + 3ax + ay + 3bx + by = (3x + 3ax + 3bx) + (y + ay + by)
= 3x(1 + a + b) + y(1 + a + b)
Take out the common factor (1 + a + b):
= (3x + y)(1 + a + b)

Q: 7. 2y⁵ + 3y⁴ + 2y³ + 3y² + 6y + 9

Ans: 2y⁵ + 3y⁴ + 2y³ + 3y² + 6y + 9
= (2y⁵ + 3y⁴) + (2y³ + 3y²) + (6y + 9)
= y⁴(2y + 3) + y²(2y + 3) + 3(2y + 3)
Take out the common factor (2y + 3):
= (2y + 3)(y⁴ + y² + 3)

Q: 8. x² − xy + xz + 3x − 3y − yz

Ans: x² − xy + xz + 3x − 3y − yz
= (x² − xy) + (xz − yz) + (3x − 3y)
= x(x − y) + z(x − y) + 3(x − y)
Take out the common factor (x − y):
= (x − y)(x + z + 3)

mcqs.q: Factorize x² + xy + xz + yz.
mcqs.why: Group in pairs. Step 1: (x² + xy) + (xz + yz) = x(x + y) + z(x + y). Step 2: the common factor is (x + y). Step 3: take it out to get (x + y)(x + z).

mcqs.q: Factorize a² + 2a + ab + 2b.
mcqs.why: Group in pairs. Step 1: (a² + 2a) + (ab + 2b) = a(a + 2) + b(a + 2). Step 2: the common factor is (a + 2). Step 3: the factorization is (a + 2)(a + b).

mcqs.q: Factorize a² − 2b³ − 2ab² + ab.
mcqs.why: Rearrange and group. Step 1: (a² + ab) − (2ab² + 2b³) = a(a + b) − 2b²(a + b). Step 2: the common factor is (a + b). Step 3: take it out: (a + b)(a − 2b²).

mcqs.q: Factorize ax − a − x + 1.
mcqs.why: Group in pairs. Step 1: (ax − a) − (x − 1) = a(x − 1) − 1(x − 1). Step 2: the common factor is (x − 1). Step 3: take it out to get (x − 1)(a − 1).

mcqs.q: Factorize 3x³ − 2x² + 18x − 12.
mcqs.why: Group in pairs. Step 1: (3x³ − 2x²) + (18x − 12) = x²(3x − 2) + 6(3x − 2). Step 2: the common factor is (3x − 2). Step 3: the result is (3x − 2)(x² + 6).

mcqs.q: Factorize 3x + y + 3ax + ay + 3bx + by.
mcqs.why: Collect terms with x and with y. Step 1: (3x + 3ax + 3bx) + (y + ay + by) = 3x(1 + a + b) + y(1 + a + b). Step 2: common factor (1 + a + b). Step 3: (3x + y)(1 + a + b).

mcqs.q: Factorize 2y⁵ + 3y⁴ + 2y³ + 3y² + 6y + 9.
mcqs.why: Group in three pairs. Step 1: y⁴(2y + 3) + y²(2y + 3) + 3(2y + 3). Step 2: the common factor is (2y + 3). Step 3: take it out: (2y + 3)(y⁴ + y² + 3).

mcqs.q: Factorize x² − xy + xz + 3x − 3y − yz.
mcqs.why: Group to make (x − y). Step 1: x(x − y) + z(x − y) + 3(x − y) from the three pairs. Step 2: the common factor is (x − y). Step 3: the factorization is (x − y)(x + z + 3).

mcqs.q: In x² + xy + xz + yz = x(x + y) + z(x + y), the common binomial factor is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: the first pair x² + xy gives x(x + y). Step 2: the second pair xz + yz gives z(x + y). Step 3: both pairs contain the same binomial (x + y), so it is the common factor taken out next.

mcqs.q: In 3x³ − 2x² + 18x − 12, after grouping the common binomial factor is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: (3x³ − 2x²) = x²(3x − 2). Step 2: (18x − 12) = 6(3x − 2). Step 3: the binomial appearing in both groups is (3x − 2), which is then taken out as the common factor.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Perfect square trinomials: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)² and a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)².
  • Check the middle term: it must be twice the product of the two square roots, e.g. x² + 4x + 4 has 2(x)(2) = 4x, so it is (x + 2)².
  • 9a² + 12ab + 4b² = (3a + 2b)² because (3a)² = 9a², 2(3a)(2b) = 12ab and (2b)² = 4b².
  • Take out a common factor first when needed: −2x² + 12x − 18 = −2(x² − 6x + 9) = −2(x − 3)².
  • 49y² − 14yz + z² = (7y − z)² and 16a² − 24ab + 9b² = (4a − 3b)².
  • Compound terms work the same way: 25(a + b)² − 20(a + b)c + 4c² = (5a + 5b − 2c)².

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Factorize: x² + 4x + 4

Ans: Formula: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)²
x² + 4x + 4 = (x)² + 2(x)(2) + (2)²
= (x + 2)²
= (x + 2)(x + 2)

Q: 2. y² − 8y + 16

Ans: Formula: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)²
y² − 8y + 16 = (y)² − 2(y)(4) + (4)²
= (y − 4)²
= (y − 4)(y − 4)

Q: 3. 9a² + 12ab + 4b²

Ans: Formula: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)²
9a² + 12ab + 4b² = (3a)² + 2(3a)(2b) + (2b)²
= (3a + 2b)²
= (3a + 2b)(3a + 2b)

Q: 4. −2x² + 12x − 18

Ans: Take out the common factor −2:
−2x² + 12x − 18 = −2(x² − 6x + 9)
Formula: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)²
x² − 6x + 9 = (x)² − 2(x)(3) + (3)² = (x − 3)²
So −2x² + 12x − 18 = −2(x − 3)(x − 3)

Q: 5. 25(a + b)² − 20(a + b)c + 4c²

Ans: Formula: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)², with a = 5(a + b) and b = 2c:
25(a + b)² − 20(a + b)c + 4c²
= (5(a + b))² − 2(5(a + b))(2c) + (2c)²
= (5(a + b) − 2c)²
= (5a + 5b − 2c)(5a + 5b − 2c)

Q: 6. 49y² − 14yz + z²

Ans: Formula: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)²
49y² − 14yz + z² = (7y)² − 2(7y)(z) + (z)²
= (7y − z)²
= (7y − z)(7y − z)

Q: 7. 16a² + 9b² − 24ab

Ans: Arrange the terms:
16a² + 9b² − 24ab = 16a² − 24ab + 9b²
Formula: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)²
= (4a)² − 2(4a)(3b) + (3b)²
= (4a − 3b)²
= (4a − 3b)(4a − 3b)

Q: 8. 4x² + 4 + 1/x²

Ans: Formula: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)², with a = 2x and b = 1/x:
4x² + 4 + 1/x² = (2x)² + 2(2x)(1/x) + (1/x)²
= (2x + 1/x)²
= (2x + 1/x)(2x + 1/x)

mcqs.q: Factorize x² + 4x + 4.
mcqs.why: Use a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)². Step 1: x² = (x)² and 4 = (2)². Step 2: check the middle term: 2(x)(2) = 4x, which matches. Step 3: x² + 4x + 4 = (x + 2)².

mcqs.q: Factorize y² − 8y + 16.
mcqs.why: Use a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)². Step 1: y² = (y)² and 16 = (4)². Step 2: check: 2(y)(4) = 8y, matching the middle term with a minus sign. Step 3: the result is (y − 4)².

mcqs.q: Factorize 9a² + 12ab + 4b².
mcqs.why: Use a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)² with a = 3a and b = 2b. Step 1: (3a)² = 9a² and (2b)² = 4b². Step 2: 2(3a)(2b) = 12ab matches the middle term. Step 3: the square is (3a + 2b)².

mcqs.q: Factorize −2x² + 12x − 18.
mcqs.why: Step 1: take out the common factor −2: −2(x² − 6x + 9). Step 2: inside, (x)² − 2(x)(3) + (3)² matches a² − 2ab + b². Step 3: this is (x − 3)², so the answer is −2(x − 3)².

mcqs.q: Factorize 25(a + b)² − 20(a + b)c + 4c².
mcqs.why: Use a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)² with a = 5(a + b) and b = 2c. Step 1: (5(a + b))² = 25(a + b)² and (2c)² = 4c². Step 2: 2·5(a + b)·2c = 20(a + b)c matches. Step 3: the square is (5(a + b) − 2c)² = (5a + 5b − 2c)².

mcqs.q: Factorize 49y² − 14yz + z².
mcqs.why: Use a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)². Step 1: 49y² = (7y)² and z² = (z)². Step 2: check the middle term: 2(7y)(z) = 14yz, with a minus sign. Step 3: the factorization is (7y − z)².

mcqs.q: Factorize 16a² + 9b² − 24ab.
mcqs.why: Step 1: rearrange as 16a² − 24ab + 9b². Step 2: (4a)² = 16a², (3b)² = 9b² and 2(4a)(3b) = 24ab matches the middle term. Step 3: by a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)² the result is (4a − 3b)².

mcqs.q: Factorize 4x² + 4 + 1/x².
mcqs.why: Use a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)² with a = 2x and b = 1/x. Step 1: (2x)² = 4x² and (1/x)² = 1/x². Step 2: 2(2x)(1/x) = 4 matches the middle term. Step 3: the square is (2x + 1/x)².

mcqs.q: The identity a² + 2ab + b² equals:
mcqs.why: Step 1: expand (a + b)² = (a + b)(a + b). Step 2: this gives a² + ab + ab + b². Step 3: combining the middle terms gives a² + 2ab + b², so a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)².

mcqs.q: The middle term of (3a + 2b)² is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: in (a + b)² the middle term is 2ab. Step 2: here a is replaced by 3a and b by 2b, so the middle term is 2(3a)(2b). Step 3: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12, giving 12ab, which matches 9a² + 12ab + 4b².

lessons.title: Exercise 2.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Difference of two squares: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
  • 16x² − 9 = (4x + 3)(4x − 3) and 16 − 25x² = (4 + 5x)(4 − 5x).
  • Take out a common factor first when present: 2x² − 288 = 2(x² − 144) = 2(x + 12)(x − 12).
  • x³y − xy³ = xy(x² − y²) = xy(x + y)(x − y).
  • Apply the formula repeatedly: x⁸ − y⁸ = (x⁴ + y⁴)(x² + y²)(x + y)(x − y).
  • (81/16)x⁴ − 625 needs the formula twice: ((9/4)x² + 25)((3/2)x + 5)((3/2)x − 5).

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Factorize: 16x² − 9

Ans: Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
16x² − 9 = (4x)² − (3)²
= (4x + 3)(4x − 3)

Q: 2. x³y − xy³

Ans: Take out the common factor xy:
x³y − xy³ = xy(x² − y²)
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= xy(x + y)(x − y)

Q: 3. 2x² − 288

Ans: Take out the common factor 2:
2x² − 288 = 2(x² − 144)
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
x² − 144 = (x)² − (12)² = (x + 12)(x − 12)
So 2x² − 288 = 2(x + 12)(x − 12)

Q: 4. 2(x − y)a² − 18(x − y)

Ans: Take out the common factor 2(x − y):
2(x − y)a² − 18(x − y) = 2(x − y)(a² − 9)
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
a² − 9 = (a + 3)(a − 3)
So the expression = 2(x − y)(a + 3)(a − 3)

Q: 5. x²/y² − y²/x²

Ans: Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), with a = x/y and b = y/x:
x²/y² − y²/x² = (x/y)² − (y/x)²
= (x/y + y/x)(x/y − y/x)

Q: 6. (81/16)x⁴ − 625

Ans: Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
(81/16)x⁴ − 625 = ((9/4)x²)² − (25)²
= ((9/4)x² + 25)((9/4)x² − 25)
Apply the formula again to (9/4)x² − 25 = ((3/2)x)² − (5)²:
= ((9/4)x² + 25)((3/2)x + 5)((3/2)x − 5)

Q: 7. 16 − 25x²

Ans: Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
16 − 25x² = (4)² − (5x)²
= (4 + 5x)(4 − 5x)

Q: 8. ab³ + 2b² − ab − 2

Ans: Group the terms:
ab³ + 2b² − ab − 2 = (ab³ − ab) + (2b² − 2)
= ab(b² − 1) + 2(b² − 1)
Take out the common factor (b² − 1):
= (b² − 1)(ab + 2)
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (b + 1)(b − 1)(ab + 2)

Q: 9. 9y² − 64x²

Ans: Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
9y² − 64x² = (3y)² − (8x)²
= (3y + 8x)(3y − 8x)

Q: 10. x⁸ − y⁸

Ans: Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), applied repeatedly:
x⁸ − y⁸ = (x⁴)² − (y⁴)² = (x⁴ + y⁴)(x⁴ − y⁴)
x⁴ − y⁴ = (x² + y²)(x² − y²) = (x² + y²)(x + y)(x − y)
So x⁸ − y⁸ = (x⁴ + y⁴)(x² + y²)(x + y)(x − y)

mcqs.q: Factorize 16x² − 9.
mcqs.why: Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). Step 1: 16x² = (4x)² and 9 = (3)². Step 2: write the sum and difference factors. Step 3: 16x² − 9 = (4x + 3)(4x − 3).

mcqs.q: Factorize x³y − xy³.
mcqs.why: Step 1: take out the common factor xy: xy(x² − y²). Step 2: apply a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) to x² − y². Step 3: x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y), so the result is xy(x + y)(x − y).

mcqs.q: Factorize 2x² − 288.
mcqs.why: Step 1: take out the common factor 2: 2(x² − 144). Step 2: 144 = (12)², so x² − 144 is a difference of squares. Step 3: x² − 144 = (x + 12)(x − 12), giving 2(x + 12)(x − 12).

mcqs.q: Factorize 2(x − y)a² − 18(x − y).
mcqs.why: Step 1: take out the common factor 2(x − y): 2(x − y)(a² − 9). Step 2: a² − 9 = (a)² − (3)² is a difference of squares. Step 3: a² − 9 = (a + 3)(a − 3), so the full result is 2(x − y)(a + 3)(a − 3).

mcqs.q: Factorize x²/y² − y²/x².
mcqs.why: Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) with a = x/y and b = y/x. Step 1: (x/y)² = x²/y² and (y/x)² = y²/x². Step 2: write sum and difference. Step 3: the factorization is (x/y + y/x)(x/y − y/x).

mcqs.q: Factorize (81/16)x⁴ − 625 completely.
mcqs.why: Step 1: (81/16)x⁴ = ((9/4)x²)² and 625 = (25)², so the difference of squares gives ((9/4)x² + 25)((9/4)x² − 25). Step 2: (9/4)x² − 25 = ((3/2)x)² − (5)². Step 3: factorize it again as ((3/2)x + 5)((3/2)x − 5).

mcqs.q: Factorize 16 − 25x².
mcqs.why: Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). Step 1: 16 = (4)² and 25x² = (5x)². Step 2: write the sum factor (4 + 5x) and the difference factor (4 − 5x). Step 3: 16 − 25x² = (4 + 5x)(4 − 5x).

mcqs.q: Factorize ab³ + 2b² − ab − 2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: group: (ab³ − ab) + (2b² − 2) = ab(b² − 1) + 2(b² − 1). Step 2: take out (b² − 1): (b² − 1)(ab + 2). Step 3: b² − 1 = (b + 1)(b − 1) by the difference of squares, giving (b + 1)(b − 1)(ab + 2).

mcqs.q: Factorize 9y² − 64x².
mcqs.why: Use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). Step 1: 9y² = (3y)² and 64x² = (8x)². Step 2: write the sum and difference factors. Step 3: 9y² − 64x² = (3y + 8x)(3y − 8x).

mcqs.q: Factorize x⁸ − y⁸ completely.
mcqs.why: Apply a² − b² repeatedly. Step 1: x⁸ − y⁸ = (x⁴ + y⁴)(x⁴ − y⁴). Step 2: x⁴ − y⁴ = (x² + y²)(x² − y²). Step 3: x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y). Combining gives (x⁴ + y⁴)(x² + y²)(x + y)(x − y).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.5
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Method: three terms form a perfect square and the fourth is a square, then use a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
  • x² − 2xy + y² − 4 = (x − y)² − 2² = (x − y + 2)(x − y − 2).
  • Group with a minus sign when needed: 1 − a² + 2ab − b² = 1 − (a − b)² = (1 + a − b)(1 − a + b).
  • 1 + 2xy − y² − x² = 1 − (x − y)² = (1 + x − y)(1 − x + y).
  • Two squares can be subtracted: (a + b)² − (c − d)² = (a + b + c − d)(a + b − c + d).
  • −a² + b² − 2b + 1 = (b − 1)² − a² = (b − 1 + a)(b − 1 − a).

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Factorize: x² − 2xy + y² − 4

Ans: The first three terms form a perfect square:
x² − 2xy + y² − 4 = (x − y)² − (2)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (x − y + 2)(x − y − 2)

Q: 2. 9a²b² − 12abc + 4c² − 25d²

Ans: The first three terms form a perfect square:
9a²b² − 12abc + 4c² = (3ab)² − 2(3ab)(2c) + (2c)² = (3ab − 2c)²
So the expression = (3ab − 2c)² − (5d)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (3ab − 2c + 5d)(3ab − 2c − 5d)

Q: 3. 1 − a² + 2ab − b²

Ans: Group the last three terms:
1 − a² + 2ab − b² = 1 − (a² − 2ab + b²)
= 1 − (a − b)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (1 + a − b)(1 − a + b)

Q: 4. 1 + 2xy − y² − x²

Ans: Group the terms:
1 + 2xy − y² − x² = 1 − (x² − 2xy + y²)
= 1 − (x − y)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (1 + x − y)(1 − x + y)

Q: 5. a² + 2ab + b² − c² + 2cd − d²

Ans: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)² and c² − 2cd + d² = (c − d)²
So the expression = (a + b)² − (c − d)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (a + b + c − d)(a + b − c + d)

Q: 6. 2(xy + pq) − x² − y² + p² + q²

Ans: Expand the first term and regroup:
2(xy + pq) − x² − y² + p² + q²
= (p² + 2pq + q²) − (x² − 2xy + y²)
= (p + q)² − (x − y)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (p + q + x − y)(p + q − x + y)

Q: 7. −a² + b² − 2b + 1

Ans: Group the last three terms:
−a² + b² − 2b + 1 = (b² − 2b + 1) − a²
= (b − 1)² − a²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (b − 1 + a)(b − 1 − a)

Q: 8. 25a²b² − 20abc + 4c² − 16d²

Ans: The first three terms form a perfect square:
25a²b² − 20abc + 4c² = (5ab)² − 2(5ab)(2c) + (2c)² = (5ab − 2c)²
So the expression = (5ab − 2c)² − (4d)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (5ab − 2c + 4d)(5ab − 2c − 4d)

mcqs.q: Factorize x² − 2xy + y² − 4.
mcqs.why: Step 1: the first three terms are a perfect square: x² − 2xy + y² = (x − y)². Step 2: the expression becomes (x − y)² − (2)². Step 3: by a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) this is (x − y + 2)(x − y − 2).

mcqs.q: Factorize 9a²b² − 12abc + 4c² − 25d².
mcqs.why: Step 1: 9a²b² − 12abc + 4c² = (3ab)² − 2(3ab)(2c) + (2c)² = (3ab − 2c)². Step 2: the expression is (3ab − 2c)² − (5d)². Step 3: difference of squares gives (3ab − 2c + 5d)(3ab − 2c − 5d).

mcqs.q: Factorize 1 − a² + 2ab − b².
mcqs.why: Step 1: group the last three terms: 1 − (a² − 2ab + b²). Step 2: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)², so we have 1 − (a − b)². Step 3: difference of squares: (1 + a − b)(1 − a + b).

mcqs.q: Factorize 1 + 2xy − y² − x².
mcqs.why: Step 1: rewrite as 1 − (x² − 2xy + y²). Step 2: x² − 2xy + y² = (x − y)², giving 1 − (x − y)². Step 3: by a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) this is (1 + x − y)(1 − x + y).

mcqs.q: Factorize a² + 2ab + b² − c² + 2cd − d².
options: (a + b + c − d)(a + b − c + d)
(a + b − c − d)(a + b + c + d)
(a − b + c − d)(a − b − c + d)
mcqs.why: Step 1: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)² and c² − 2cd + d² = (c − d)². Step 2: the expression is (a + b)² − (c − d)². Step 3: difference of squares gives (a + b + c − d)(a + b − c + d).

mcqs.q: Factorize 2(xy + pq) − x² − y² + p² + q².
options: (p − q + x − y)(p − q − x + y)
(p + q + x − y)(p + q − x + y)
(x + y + p + q)(x + y − p − q)
mcqs.why: Step 1: expand and regroup: (p² + 2pq + q²) − (x² − 2xy + y²). Step 2: this is (p + q)² − (x − y)². Step 3: difference of squares gives (p + q + x − y)(p + q − x + y).

mcqs.q: Factorize −a² + b² − 2b + 1.
mcqs.why: Step 1: group: (b² − 2b + 1) − a². Step 2: b² − 2b + 1 = (b − 1)², so we have (b − 1)² − a². Step 3: difference of squares gives (b − 1 + a)(b − 1 − a).

mcqs.q: Factorize 25a²b² − 20abc + 4c² − 16d².
mcqs.why: Step 1: 25a²b² − 20abc + 4c² = (5ab)² − 2(5ab)(2c) + (2c)² = (5ab − 2c)². Step 2: the expression is (5ab − 2c)² − (4d)². Step 3: difference of squares gives (5ab − 2c + 4d)(5ab − 2c − 4d).

mcqs.q: The first step in factorizing x² − 2xy + y² − 4 is to write it as:
mcqs.why: Step 1: recognize x² − 2xy + y² as (x)² − 2(x)(y) + (y)². Step 2: by a² − 2ab + b² this equals (x − y)². Step 3: the remaining term −4 is −(2)², so the whole expression is (x − y)² − 2².

mcqs.q: 1 − a² + 2ab − b² can first be written as:
mcqs.why: Step 1: take the last three terms together with a minus sign: −a² + 2ab − b² = −(a² − 2ab + b²). Step 2: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)². Step 3: therefore the expression is 1 − (a − b)², ready for the difference of squares.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.6
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Type a⁴ + 4b⁴: add and subtract 4a²b² to complete a square, then use the difference of squares.
  • x⁴ + 4 = (x² + 2)² − (2x)² = (x² + 2x + 2)(x² − 2x + 2); the term added and subtracted is 4x².
  • 4x⁴ + 81 = (2x² + 9)² − (6x)² = (2x² + 6x + 9)(2x² − 6x + 9).
  • Type a⁴ + a²b² + b⁴: add and subtract a²b², e.g. x⁴ + x² + 1 = (x² + 1)² − x² = (x² + x + 1)(x² − x + 1).
  • x⁸ + x⁴ + 1 factorizes further to (x² + x + 1)(x² − x + 1)(x⁴ − x² + 1).
  • 16x⁴ + 4x²y² + y⁴ = (4x² + y²)² − (2xy)² = (4x² + 2xy + y²)(4x² − 2xy + y²).

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Factorize: x⁴ + 4

Ans: This is of the type a⁴ + 4b⁴. Add and subtract 4x² to make a perfect square:
x⁴ + 4 = x⁴ + 4x² + 4 − 4x²
= (x² + 2)² − (2x)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (x² + 2x + 2)(x² − 2x + 2)

Q: 2. 4x⁴ + 81

Ans: Add and subtract 2(2x²)(9) = 36x² to make a perfect square:
4x⁴ + 81 = (2x²)² + 2(2x²)(9) + (9)² − 36x²
= (2x² + 9)² − (6x)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (2x² + 6x + 9)(2x² − 6x + 9)

Q: 3. 4p⁴ + q⁴

Ans: Add and subtract 4p²q² to make a perfect square:
4p⁴ + q⁴ = (2p²)² + 2(2p²)(q²) + (q²)² − 4p²q²
= (2p² + q²)² − (2pq)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (2p² + 2pq + q²)(2p² − 2pq + q²)

Q: 4. x⁴ + x² + 1

Ans: This is of the type a⁴ + a²b² + b⁴. Add and subtract x²:
x⁴ + x² + 1 = x⁴ + 2x² + 1 − x²
= (x² + 1)² − (x)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (x² + x + 1)(x² − x + 1)

Q: 5. x⁸ + x⁴ + 1

Ans: Add and subtract x⁴ to make a perfect square:
x⁸ + x⁴ + 1 = (x⁴)² + 2(x⁴)(1) + (1)² − x⁴
= (x⁴ + 1)² − (x²)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (x⁴ + x² + 1)(x⁴ − x² + 1)
Factorize x⁴ + x² + 1 as in Q4:
= (x² + x + 1)(x² − x + 1)(x⁴ − x² + 1)

Q: 6. x⁴ + 1/x⁴ − 7

Ans: Complete the square on x⁴ + 1/x⁴:
x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (x² + 1/x²)² − 2
So x⁴ + 1/x⁴ − 7 = (x² + 1/x²)² − 9
= (x² + 1/x²)² − (3)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (x² + 1/x² + 3)(x² + 1/x² − 3)

Q: 7. 16x⁴ + 4x²y² + y⁴

Ans: Add and subtract 4x²y² to make a perfect square:
16x⁴ + 4x²y² + y⁴ = (4x²)² + 2(4x²)(y²) + (y²)² − 4x²y²
= (4x² + y²)² − (2xy)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (4x² + 2xy + y²)(4x² − 2xy + y²)

Q: 8. 4a⁵b + 11a³b³ + 9ab⁵

Ans: Take out the common factor ab:
4a⁵b + 11a³b³ + 9ab⁵ = ab(4a⁴ + 11a²b² + 9b⁴)
In the bracket, add and subtract a²b² to make a perfect square:
4a⁴ + 11a²b² + 9b⁴ = (2a² + 3b²)² − (ab)²
Formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
= (2a² + ab + 3b²)(2a² − ab + 3b²)
So the expression = ab(2a² + 3b² + ab)(2a² + 3b² − ab)

mcqs.q: Factorize x⁴ + 4.
mcqs.why: This is type a⁴ + 4b⁴. Step 1: add and subtract 4x²: x⁴ + 4x² + 4 − 4x². Step 2: this is (x² + 2)² − (2x)². Step 3: difference of squares gives (x² + 2x + 2)(x² − 2x + 2).

mcqs.q: Factorize 4x⁴ + 81.
mcqs.why: Step 1: add and subtract 36x²: (2x²)² + 2(2x²)(9) + (9)² − 36x². Step 2: this is (2x² + 9)² − (6x)². Step 3: difference of squares gives (2x² + 6x + 9)(2x² − 6x + 9).
