mcqs.why: Factorize a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²). The second expression, a² + ab + b², appears as a factor of the first, so it is the highest common factor: H.C.F = a² + ab + b². This is the book's own keyed answer.

mcqs.q: The H.C.F of 8a³ − b³ and 4a² − 4ab + b² is:
mcqs.why: Factorize: 8a³ − b³ = (2a − b)(4a² + 2ab + b²) using a³ − b³ with 2a and b, and 4a² − 4ab + b² = (2a − b)². The common factor is (2a − b), so H.C.F = 2a − b. This is the book's own keyed answer.

mcqs.q: The L.C.M of (a − b)³ and (a − b)⁴ is:
mcqs.why: For powers of the same base, the L.C.M takes the higher power, because (a − b)⁴ = (a − b)³ × (a − b) is divisible by both. So L.C.M = (a − b)⁴. This is the book's own keyed answer.

mcqs.q: x/(x − y) − y/(x + y) equals:
mcqs.why: Use the common denominator (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y². The numerator is x(x + y) − y(x − y) = x² + xy − xy + y² = x² + y². So the result is (x² + y²)/(x² − y²). This is the book's own keyed answer.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Review: by division, x³ + 4x² + 4x + 3 and x³ + 2x² − 4x − 3 have H.C.F x + 3 (the last divisor when the remainder becomes 0).
  • Review: x³ + 6x² + 11x + 6 = (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3) and x³ + 3x² − x − 3 = (x + 3)(x + 1)(x − 1), so their L.C.M is (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)(x − 1).
  • Review: L = (A × B)/H; dividing the product by the H.C.F gives the L.C.M.
  • Review: before simplifying fractions, factorize the denominators and cancel each numerator factor against its matching denominator factor.
  • Review: a product of quadratics is a perfect square when each linear factor appears an even number of times.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Find H.C.F of x³ + 4x² + 4x + 3 and x³ + 2x² − 4x − 3 by division method.

Ans: By the division method:
Divide x³ + 4x² + 4x + 3 by x³ + 2x² − 4x − 3: quotient 1, remainder 2x² + 8x + 6 = 2(x² + 4x + 3).
Divide x³ + 2x² − 4x − 3 by (x² + 4x + 3): quotient x − 2, remainder x + 3.
Divide x² + 4x + 3 by (x + 3): quotient x + 1, remainder 0.
The last divisor is the H.C.F.
H.C.F = x + 3

Q: 2. Find L.C.M of x³ + 6x² + 11x + 6 and x³ + 3x² − x − 3.

Ans: Factorize both polynomials:
x³ + 6x² + 11x + 6: putting x = −1 gives 0, so (x + 1) is a factor; dividing gives x² + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3). So it is (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3).
x³ + 3x² − x − 3 = x²(x + 3) − 1(x + 3) = (x + 3)(x + 1)(x − 1).
L.C.M = (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)(x − 1)

Q: 3. If the product of two polynomials is x⁴ + 5x³ − 6x² − 2x − 28 and their H.C.F is x − 2, find the L.C.M.

Ans: Formula: A × B = H × L, so L = (A × B)/H.
Divide x⁴ + 5x³ − 6x² − 2x − 28 by (x − 2):
Using synthetic division with 2: coefficients 1, 5, −6, −2, −28 give quotient coefficients 1, 7, 8, 14 and remainder 0.
L.C.M = x³ + 7x² + 8x + 14

Q: 4. Simplify: (x − 5)/(x² − 7x + 10) − 2(x − 6)/(x² − 9x + 18) + (x − 7)/(x² − 4x − 21)

Ans: Factorize the denominators:
x² − 7x + 10 = (x − 5)(x − 2)
x² − 9x + 18 = (x − 6)(x − 3)
x² − 4x − 21 = (x − 7)(x + 3)
So the expression = 1/(x − 2) − 2/(x − 3) + 1/(x + 3).
L.C.M of denominators = (x − 2)(x − 3)(x + 3).
Numerator: (x − 3)(x + 3) − 2(x − 2)(x + 3) + (x − 2)(x − 3)
= (x² − 9) − 2(x² + x − 6) + (x² − 5x + 6)
= −7x + 9
= (9 − 7x)/((x − 2)(x − 3)(x + 3))

Q: 5. Simplify: (x³ − 8)/(2x²) × 4x/(x² − 5x + 6)

Ans: Factorize: x³ − 8 = (x − 2)(x² + 2x + 4) and x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3).
= [(x − 2)(x² + 2x + 4) × 4x]/[2x² × (x − 2)(x − 3)]
Cancel (x − 2) and 2x:
= 2(x² + 2x + 4)/(x(x − 3))

Q: 6. Simplify: 5/(x − 1) ÷ 25(x − 2)/(x − 1)

Ans: Division rule: A/B ÷ C/D = A/B × D/C.
= 5/(x − 1) × (x − 1)/(25(x − 2))
Cancel (x − 1):
= 5/(25(x − 2))
= 1/(5(x − 2))

Q: 7. Find the square root of (x² + 6x + 5)(x² + 9x + 9)(x² + 13x + 40) by factorization.

Ans: Note: the middle factor is printed as x² + 9x + 9, which does not factorize; the book's answer key gives ±(x + 1)(x + 5)(x + 8), which fits x² + 9x + 8 = (x + 1)(x + 8). The constant 9 is a misprint for 8. Solving with the corrected factor:
x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 1)(x + 5)
x² + 9x + 8 = (x + 1)(x + 8)
x² + 13x + 40 = (x + 5)(x + 8)
Product = (x + 1)²(x + 5)²(x + 8)² = [(x + 1)(x + 5)(x + 8)]²
Square root = ±(x + 1)(x + 5)(x + 8)

mcqs.q: Find the H.C.F of x³ + 4x² + 4x + 3 and x³ + 2x² − 4x − 3 by the division method.
mcqs.why: Divide x³ + 4x² + 4x + 3 by x³ + 2x² − 4x − 3: quotient 1, remainder 2x² + 8x + 6 = 2(x² + 4x + 3). Divide x³ + 2x² − 4x − 3 by (x² + 4x + 3): quotient x − 2, remainder x + 3. Divide x² + 4x + 3 by (x + 3): quotient x + 1, remainder 0. The last divisor is the H.C.F: x + 3.

mcqs.q: Find the L.C.M of x³ + 6x² + 11x + 6 and x³ + 3x² − x − 3.
mcqs.why: Factorize: putting x = −1 gives 0 for the first, and dividing gives x² + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3), so it is (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3). The second: x²(x + 3) − 1(x + 3) = (x + 3)(x + 1)(x − 1). Take common factors (x + 1), (x + 3) once with non-common (x + 2), (x − 1).

mcqs.q: The product of two polynomials is x⁴ + 5x³ − 6x² − 2x − 28 and their H.C.F is x − 2. Find the L.C.M.
mcqs.why: Use L = (A × B)/H. Divide x⁴ + 5x³ − 6x² − 2x − 28 by (x − 2) using synthetic division with 2: coefficients 1, 5, −6, −2, −28 give quotient coefficients 1, 7, 8, 14 and remainder 0. So L.C.M = x³ + 7x² + 8x + 14.

Factorize denominators: x² − 7x + 10 = (x − 5)(x − 2), x² − 9x + 18 = (x − 6)(x − 3), x² − 4x − 21 = (x − 7)(x + 3), so the fractions become 1/(x − 2) − 2/(x − 3) + 1/(x + 3). With L.C.M (x − 2)(x − 3)(x + 3), the numerator is (x − 3)(x + 3) − 2(x − 2)(x + 3) + (x − 2)(x − 3) = (x² − 9) − 2(x² + x − 6) + (x² − 5x + 6) = −7x + 9.

mcqs.q: Simplify: (x³ − 8)/(2x²) × 4x/(x² − 5x + 6)
mcqs.why: Factorize: x³ − 8 = (x − 2)(x² + 2x + 4) and x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3). The product is [(x − 2)(x² + 2x + 4) × 4x]/[2x² × (x − 2)(x − 3)]. Cancel (x − 2) and divide numerator and denominator by 2x: result = 2(x² + 2x + 4)/(x(x − 3)).
By the division rule, the expression becomes 5/(x − 1) × (x − 1)/(25(x − 2)). Cancel (x − 1): 5/(25(x − 2)). Dividing numerator and denominator by 5 gives 1/(5(x − 2)).

mcqs.q: Find the square root of (x² + 6x + 5)(x² + 9x + 8)(x² + 13x + 40) by factorization.
mcqs.why: Factorize: x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 1)(x + 5); x² + 9x + 8 = (x + 1)(x + 8); x² + 13x + 40 = (x + 5)(x + 8). The product is (x + 1)²(x + 5)²(x + 8)² = [(x + 1)(x + 5)(x + 8)]², so the square root is ±(x + 1)(x + 5)(x + 8). Note: the book prints the middle factor as x² + 9x + 9, which does not factorize; the constant 9 is a misprint for 8, as the book's own key confirms.

mcqs.q: In Review Q4, (x − 5)/(x² − 7x + 10) simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Factorize the denominator: x² − 7x + 10 = (x − 5)(x − 2), since 5 × 2 = 10 and 5 + 2 = 7. So (x − 5)/((x − 5)(x − 2)) = 1/(x − 2) after cancelling (x − 5).

mcqs.q: In Review Q4, 2(x − 6)/(x² − 9x + 18) simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Factorize the denominator: x² − 9x + 18 = (x − 6)(x − 3), since 6 × 3 = 18 and 6 + 3 = 9. So 2(x − 6)/((x − 6)(x − 3)) = 2/(x − 3) after cancelling (x − 6).

mcqs.q: Which relation connects two polynomials A and B with their H.C.F H and L.C.M L?
mcqs.why: For two polynomials, the product of the polynomials equals the product of their H.C.F and L.C.M: A × B = H × L. This gives the working formulas L = (A × B)/H, H = (A × B)/L and B = (H × L)/A used throughout this unit.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A linear equation is solved by doing the same operation to both sides: add or subtract the same quantity, then divide by the coefficient of x.
  • Always verify the answer by substituting it back into the original equation.
  • With fractions, multiply every term by the L.C.M of the denominators to clear them (12 for denominators 3, 2, 4, 12 in Q6).
  • Consecutive numbers are x, x + 1; consecutive odd integers are x, x + 2, x + 4.
  • For a rectangle, perimeter = 2(length + breadth).
  • In digit problems, a two-digit number with ten's digit t and unit's digit u is 10t + u; reversing the digits gives 10u + t.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Solve and verify: 3x − 5 = 7

Ans: Add 5 to both sides:
3x − 5 + 5 = 7 + 5
3x = 12
Divide both sides by 3:
x = 4
Verification: 3(4) − 5 = 12 − 5 = 7 ✓
Solution set = {4}

Q: 2. 4(x + 2) − 2(x − 2) = 18

Ans: Expand the brackets:
4x + 8 − 2x + 4 = 18
2x + 12 = 18
Subtract 12 from both sides:
2x = 6
Divide both sides by 2:
x = 3
Verification: 4(3 + 2) − 2(3 − 2) = 20 − 2 = 18 ✓
Solution set = {3}

Q: 3. 6x + 3 = 2x + 19

Ans: Subtract 2x from both sides:
6x + 3 − 2x = 2x + 19 − 2x
4x + 3 = 19
Subtract 3 from both sides:
4x = 16
Divide both sides by 4:
x = 4
Verification: 6(4) + 3 = 27 and 2(4) + 19 = 27 ✓
Solution set = {4}

Q: 4. 1/(x − 2) = 2/(x − 1)

Ans: Cross-multiply:
1(x − 1) = 2(x − 2)
x − 1 = 2x − 4
Subtract x from both sides:
−1 = x − 4
Add 4 to both sides:
x = 3
Verification: 1/(3 − 2) = 1 and 2/(3 − 1) = 1 ✓
Solution set = {3}

Q: 5. 6x + 3 = 2x + 19 (printed identical to Q3)

Ans: Note: this question is printed exactly the same as Q3 (6x + 3 = 2x + 19), so it is solved the same way. (The book's answer key gives {−17/14} for Q5, which belongs to a different equation that is not printed here.)
Subtract 2x from both sides:
4x + 3 = 19
Subtract 3 from both sides:
4x = 16
Divide both sides by 4:
x = 4
Solution set = {4}

Q: 6. (2 + 5)/3 − ((2 − x)/2 − 1/4) = (3x + 25)/12

Ans: (2 + 5)/3 = 7/3. Multiply every term by 12 (the L.C.M of 3, 2, 4 and 12):
4(7) − 6(2 − x) + 3 = 3x + 25
28 − 12 + 6x + 3 = 3x + 25
6x + 19 = 3x + 25
Subtract 3x from both sides:
3x + 19 = 25
Subtract 19 from both sides:
3x = 6
Divide both sides by 3:
x = 2
Verification: 7/3 − (0/2 − 1/4) = 7/3 + 1/4 = 31/12 and (3(2) + 25)/12 = 31/12 ✓
Solution set = {2}

Q: 7. The sum of two consecutive numbers is 23. Find the numbers.

Ans: Let the first number be x; the next consecutive number is x + 1.
x + (x + 1) = 23
2x + 1 = 23
2x = 22
x = 11
The numbers are 11 and 12.

Q: 8. The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 159. Find the numbers.

Ans: Let the first odd integer be x; the next two are x + 2 and x + 4.
x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 159
3x + 6 = 159
3x = 153
x = 51
The numbers are 51, 53 and 55.

Q: 9. The perimeter of a rectangle is 20 m. If the length of the rectangle is 2 meter more than its breadth, find the length and breadth of the rectangle.

Ans: Let the breadth be b metres; then the length is (b + 2) metres.
Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 20
2((b + 2) + b) = 20
2(2b + 2) = 20
2b + 2 = 10
2b = 8
b = 4
Breadth = 4 m, Length = 4 + 2 = 6 m.

Q: 10. Age of mother is 13 times the age of her daughter. It will be only 5 times after four years. Find their present ages.

Ans: Let the daughter's present age be x years; the mother's present age is 13x years.
After four years: mother = 13x + 4, daughter = x + 4.
13x + 4 = 5(x + 4)
13x + 4 = 5x + 20
8x = 16
x = 2
Daughter = 2 years, Mother = 13 × 2 = 26 years.
(The book's answer key prints the mother's age as 13 years, which is the multiplier, not the age; 26 years is correct: after 4 years, 30 = 5 × 6.)

Q: 11. The sum of two digits is 10. If digits change their places, then the new number is decreased by 18 than the original number. Find the number.

Ans: Let the unit's digit be x; the ten's digit is 10 − x.
Original number = 10(10 − x) + x = 100 − 9x
New number = 10x + (10 − x) = 9x + 10
New number = original number − 18:
9x + 10 = (100 − 9x) − 18
9x + 10 = 82 − 9x
18x = 72
x = 4
Ten's digit = 10 − 4 = 6, so the number is 64.

Q: 12. Think of a number, if 4 is added to the twice of the number, the result comes to 18. Find the number.

Ans: Let the number be x.
Twice the number = 2x.
2x + 4 = 18
2x = 14
x = 7
The number is 7.

mcqs.q: Solve and verify: 3x − 5 = 7. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Add 5 to both sides: 3x − 5 + 5 = 7 + 5, so 3x = 12. Divide both sides by 3: x = 4. Verification: 3(4) − 5 = 12 − 5 = 7 ✓. Solution set = {4}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 4(x + 2) − 2(x − 2) = 18. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Expand the brackets: 4x + 8 − 2x + 4 = 18, so 2x + 12 = 18. Subtract 12 from both sides: 2x = 6. Divide both sides by 2: x = 3. Verification: 4(3 + 2) − 2(3 − 2) = 20 − 2 = 18 ✓.

mcqs.q: Solve: 6x + 3 = 2x + 19. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Subtract 2x from both sides: 6x + 3 − 2x = 19, so 4x + 3 = 19. Subtract 3 from both sides: 4x = 16. Divide both sides by 4: x = 4. Verification: 6(4) + 3 = 27 and 2(4) + 19 = 27 ✓.

mcqs.q: Solve: 1/(x − 2) = 2/(x − 1). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Cross-multiply: 1(x − 1) = 2(x − 2), so x − 1 = 2x − 4. Subtract x from both sides: −1 = x − 4. Add 4 to both sides: x = 3. Verification: 1/(3 − 2) = 1 and 2/(3 − 1) = 1 ✓.

mcqs.q: Solve: (2 + 5)/3 − ((2 − x)/2 − 1/4) = (3x + 25)/12. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: (2 + 5)/3 = 7/3. Multiply every term by 12, the L.C.M of 3, 2, 4 and 12: 4(7) − 6(2 − x) + 3 = 3x + 25, so 28 − 12 + 6x + 3 = 3x + 25, i.e. 6x + 19 = 3x + 25. Subtract 3x: 3x + 19 = 25; subtract 19: 3x = 6; divide by 3: x = 2.

mcqs.q: The sum of two consecutive numbers is 23. The numbers are:
mcqs.why: Let the first number be x; the next consecutive number is x + 1. Then x + (x + 1) = 23, so 2x + 1 = 23, 2x = 22 and x = 11. The numbers are 11 and 11 + 1 = 12. Check: 11 + 12 = 23 ✓.

mcqs.q: The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 159. The integers are:
mcqs.why: Let the first odd integer be x; the next two are x + 2 and x + 4. Then x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 159, so 3x + 6 = 159, 3x = 153 and x = 51. The integers are 51, 53 and 55. Check: 51 + 53 + 55 = 159 ✓.

mcqs.q: The perimeter of a rectangle is 20 m and its length is 2 m more than its breadth. The length and breadth are:
mcqs.why: Let the breadth be b metres; the length is (b + 2) metres. Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 20, so 2((b + 2) + b) = 20, i.e. 2(2b + 2) = 20, 2b + 2 = 10, 2b = 8, b = 4. Breadth = 4 m and length = 4 + 2 = 6 m.

mcqs.q: A mother's age is 13 times her daughter's age, and after four years it will be only 5 times. Their present ages are:
mcqs.why: Let the daughter's age be x; the mother's is 13x. After four years: 13x + 4 = 5(x + 4) = 5x + 20, so 8x = 16 and x = 2. Daughter = 2 years, mother = 13 × 2 = 26 years. Note: the book's answer key prints the mother's age as 13 years, which is the multiplier, not the age — that key is wrong; check: after 4 years, 30 = 5 × 6 ✓.

mcqs.q: Think of a number: if 4 is added to twice the number, the result is 18. The number is:
mcqs.why: Let the number be x. Twice the number is 2x, and 2x + 4 = 18. Subtract 4 from both sides: 2x = 14. Divide both sides by 2: x = 7. Check: 2(7) + 4 = 18 ✓.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A radical equation contains the unknown under a square root sign; isolate the radical, then square both sides.
  • Squaring both sides can produce an extraneous root, so every answer must be verified in the original equation.
  • A square root can never equal a negative number: √(2x + 4) = −6 has no solution.
  • If the radical is not alone, first move the other terms to the other side, e.g. √(x + 3) + 2 = 6 gives √(x + 3) = 4.
  • When both sides contain radicals, square both sides directly, e.g. √(4x − 1) = √(3x + 1) gives 4x − 1 = 3x + 1.
  • An answer that fails verification is rejected and the solution set is empty, { }.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Solve: √(x + 5) = 6

Ans: Square both sides:
(√(x + 5))² = (6)²
x + 5 = 36
x = 31
Verification: √(31 + 5) = √36 = 6 ✓
Solution set = {31}

Q: 2. √(2x + 4) = −6

Ans: Square both sides:
2x + 4 = (−6)² = 36
2x = 32
x = 16
Verification: √(2(16) + 4) = √36 = 6, which is not equal to −6.
x = 16 is an extraneous root.
Solution set = { } (no solution)

Q: 3. √(x + 3) + 2 = 6

Ans: Subtract 2 from both sides:
√(x + 3) = 4
Square both sides:
x + 3 = 16
x = 13
Verification: √(13 + 3) + 2 = 4 + 2 = 6 ✓
Solution set = {13}

Q: 4. 3√x + 7 = 10

Ans: Subtract 7 from both sides:
3√x = 3
Divide both sides by 3:
√x = 1
Square both sides:
x = 1
Verification: 3√1 + 7 = 3 + 7 = 10 ✓
Solution set = {1}

Q: 5. √(4x − 1) = √(3x + 1)

Ans: Square both sides:
4x − 1 = 3x + 1
Subtract 3x from both sides:
x − 1 = 1
x = 2
Verification: √(4(2) − 1) = √7 and √(3(2) + 1) = √7 ✓
Solution set = {2}

Q: 6. 15 − √(x + 2) = 10

Ans: Subtract 15 from both sides and change signs:
√(x + 2) = 15 − 10 = 5
Square both sides:
x + 2 = 25
x = 23
Verification: 15 − √(23 + 2) = 15 − 5 = 10 ✓
Solution set = {23}

Q: 7. √(3x − 1) + 7 = 4

Ans: Subtract 7 from both sides:
√(3x − 1) = 4 − 7 = −3
Square both sides:
3x − 1 = 9
3x = 10
x = 10/3
Verification: √(3(10/3) − 1) + 7 = √9 + 7 = 10, which is not equal to 4.
x = 10/3 is an extraneous root.
Solution set = { } (no solution)

Q: 8. √(4(2x − 1)) = 2√(x + 8)

Ans: Square both sides:
4(2x − 1) = 4(x + 8)
Divide both sides by 4:
2x − 1 = x + 8
x = 9
Verification: √(4(2(9) − 1)) = √68 = 2√17 and 2√(9 + 8) = 2√17 ✓
Solution set = {9}

mcqs.q: Solve: √(x + 5) = 6. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Square both sides: (√(x + 5))² = 6², so x + 5 = 36. Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 31. Verification: √(31 + 5) = √36 = 6 ✓. Solution set = {31}.

mcqs.q: Solve: √(2x + 4) = −6. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Squaring both sides gives 2x + 4 = (−6)² = 36, so 2x = 32 and x = 16. But verification: √(2(16) + 4) = √36 = 6, which is not equal to −6, because a square root is never negative. So x = 16 is an extraneous root and the solution set is { } (no solution).

mcqs.q: Solve: √(x + 3) + 2 = 6. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Subtract 2 from both sides to isolate the radical: √(x + 3) = 4. Square both sides: x + 3 = 16. Subtract 3: x = 13. Verification: √(13 + 3) + 2 = 4 + 2 = 6 ✓. Solution set = {13}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3√x + 7 = 10. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Subtract 7 from both sides: 3√x = 3. Divide both sides by 3: √x = 1. Square both sides: x = 1. Verification: 3√1 + 7 = 3 + 7 = 10 ✓. Solution set = {1}.

mcqs.q: Solve: √(4x − 1) = √(3x + 1). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Square both sides: 4x − 1 = 3x + 1. Subtract 3x from both sides: x − 1 = 1. Add 1 to both sides: x = 2. Verification: √(4(2) − 1) = √7 and √(3(2) + 1) = √7 ✓. Solution set = {2}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 15 − √(x + 2) = 10. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Rearrange: √(x + 2) = 15 − 10 = 5. Square both sides: x + 2 = 25. Subtract 2: x = 23. Verification: 15 − √(23 + 2) = 15 − 5 = 10 ✓. Solution set = {23}.

mcqs.q: Solve: √(3x − 1) + 7 = 4. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Subtract 7 from both sides: √(3x − 1) = 4 − 7 = −3. Squaring gives 3x − 1 = 9, so 3x = 10 and x = 10/3. But verification: √(3(10/3) − 1) + 7 = √9 + 7 = 10, which is not equal to 4. So x = 10/3 is an extraneous root and the solution set is { } (no solution).

mcqs.q: Solve: √(4(2x − 1)) = 2√(x + 8). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Square both sides: 4(2x − 1) = 4(x + 8). Divide both sides by 4: 2x − 1 = x + 8. Subtract x from both sides: x − 1 = 8, so x = 9. Verification: √(4(2(9) − 1)) = √68 = 2√17 and 2√(9 + 8) = 2√17 ✓.

mcqs.q: Why must every answer of a radical equation be verified?
options: Because squaring both sides can introduce an extraneous root that does not satisfy the original equation
Because the square root of a number is always negative
Because division by zero may occur in every step
Because linear equations have two solutions
mcqs.why: Squaring is not a reversible step: an equation like √A = −6 becomes A = 36 after squaring, whose solution makes √A = +6, not −6. Such a value satisfies the squared equation but not the original one, so it is an extraneous root and must be rejected after verification, as in √(2x + 4) = −6.

mcqs.q: Solve: √(x + 5) = 3. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Square both sides: x + 5 = 3² = 9. Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 4. Verification: √(4 + 5) = √9 = 3 ✓. Solution set = {4}.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • |A| = k (k > 0) gives two possibilities: A = k or A = −k, so an absolute value equation usually has two solutions.
  • Isolate the absolute value first: |5x − 13| + 2 = 14 gives |5x − 13| = 12 before splitting into two cases.
  • Fractions inside the modulus are handled the same way: |(x + 5)/3| = 7/2 gives (x + 5)/3 = 7/2 or (x + 5)/3 = −7/2.
  • Solution sets from this exercise: |4x| = 8 → {2, −2}; |x − 1| = 7 → {8, −6}; |x/5| = 6 → {30, −30}.
  • Each case is a simple linear equation solved by the usual balance method.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Solve: |4x| = 8

Ans: |4x| = 8 gives two possibilities:
4x = 8 or 4x = −8
x = 2 or x = −2
Solution set = {2, −2}

Q: 2. |x − 1| = 7

Ans: x − 1 = 7 or x − 1 = −7
x = 8 or x = −6
Solution set = {8, −6}

Q: 3. |x/5| = 6

Ans: x/5 = 6 or x/5 = −6
x = 30 or x = −30
Solution set = {30, −30}

Q: 4. |15x − 10| = 35

Ans: 15x − 10 = 35 or 15x − 10 = −35
15x = 45 or 15x = −25
x = 3 or x = −5/3
Solution set = {3, −5/3}

Q: 5. |(x + 5)/3| = 7/2

Ans: (x + 5)/3 = 7/2 or (x + 5)/3 = −7/2
x + 5 = 21/2 or x + 5 = −21/2
x = 21/2 − 5 = 11/2 or x = −21/2 − 5 = −31/2
Solution set = {11/2, −31/2}

Q: 6. |5x − 13| + 2 = 14

Ans: Subtract 2 from both sides:
|5x − 13| = 12
5x − 13 = 12 or 5x − 13 = −12
5x = 25 or 5x = 1
x = 5 or x = 1/5
Solution set = {5, 1/5}

Q: 7. |4x − 1| = 7

Ans: 4x − 1 = 7 or 4x − 1 = −7
4x = 8 or 4x = −6
x = 2 or x = −3/2
Solution set = {2, −3/2}

Q: 8. |9x + 11| − 2/5 = 8/5

Ans: Add 2/5 to both sides:
|9x + 11| = 8/5 + 2/5 = 2
9x + 11 = 2 or 9x + 11 = −2
9x = −9 or 9x = −13
x = −1 or x = −13/9
Solution set = {−1, −13/9}

mcqs.q: Solve: |4x| = 8. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: |4x| = 8 gives two possibilities: 4x = 8 or 4x = −8. Dividing by 4 in each case: x = 2 or x = −2. Solution set = {2, −2}.

mcqs.q: Solve: |x − 1| = 7. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: x − 1 = 7 gives x = 8; x − 1 = −7 gives x = −6. Solution set = {8, −6}.

mcqs.q: Solve: |x/5| = 6. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: x/5 = 6 gives x = 30; x/5 = −6 gives x = −30. Solution set = {30, −30}.

mcqs.q: Solve: |15x − 10| = 35. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: 15x − 10 = 35 gives 15x = 45, so x = 3; 15x − 10 = −35 gives 15x = −25, so x = −25/15 = −5/3. Solution set = {3, −5/3}.

mcqs.q: Solve: |(x + 5)/3| = 7/2. The solution set is:
Solve: |5x − 13| + 2 = 14. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: First isolate the modulus: subtract 2 from both sides, |5x − 13| = 12. Then 5x − 13 = 12 gives 5x = 25, so x = 5; and 5x − 13 = −12 gives 5x = 1, so x = 1/5. Solution set = {5, 1/5}.

mcqs.q: Solve: |4x − 1| = 7. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: 4x − 1 = 7 gives 4x = 8, so x = 2; 4x − 1 = −7 gives 4x = −6, so x = −6/4 = −3/2. Solution set = {2, −3/2}.

mcqs.q: Solve: |9x + 11| − 2/5 = 8/5. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Add 2/5 to both sides: |9x + 11| = 8/5 + 2/5 = 2. Then 9x + 11 = 2 gives 9x = −9, so x = −1; and 9x + 11 = −2 gives 9x = −13, so x = −13/9. Solution set = {−1, −13/9}.

mcqs.q: Solve: |x| − 2 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Add 2 to both sides: |x| = 2. An absolute value equation |x| = 2 gives two possibilities: x = 2 or x = −2. Solution set = {2, −2}.

mcqs.q: The equation |A| = k, where k > 0, is solved by:
mcqs.why: The absolute value |A| is the distance of A from 0, so |A| = k means A is k units from 0 in either direction: A = k or A = −k. Solving both linear equations gives the (usually two) solutions, as in |4x| = 8 giving x = 2 or x = −2.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • On a number line, > and < are shown with an open circle at the end value (the value is NOT included) and shading on the correct side.
  • ≥ and ≤ are shown with a closed (shaded) dot at the end value (the value IS included).
  • x > 0: open circle at 0, shade to the right; x < 0: open circle at 0, shade to the left.
  • For a double inequality like −5 ≤ x ≤ 6, put closed dots at both ends and shade only the part between them.
  • 3 ≥ x ≥ −2 is the same as −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; read a double inequality from the middle value x outward.
  • For 4 < x < 6 both ends have open circles because neither 4 nor 6 is included.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Depict on a number line: x > 0

Ans: On the number line: put an open circle at 0 (0 is not included) and shade the line to the right of 0, with an arrow showing it continues without end.

Q: 2. x < 0

Ans: Open circle at 0 (0 is not included); shade the line to the left of 0.

Q: 3. x ≤ 1

Ans: Closed (shaded) dot at 1 (1 is included); shade the line to the left of 1.

Q: 4. x ≤ −5

Ans: Closed (shaded) dot at −5 (−5 is included); shade the line to the left of −5.

Q: 5. x ≥ −3

Ans: Closed (shaded) dot at −3 (−3 is included); shade the line to the right of −3.

Q: 6. x ≥ 4

Ans: Closed (shaded) dot at 4 (4 is included); shade the line to the right of 4.

Q: 7. −5 ≤ x ≤ 6

Ans: Closed (shaded) dots at −5 and at 6 (both end values are included); shade the part of the line between −5 and 6.

Q: 8. 3 ≥ x ≥ −2

Ans: This is the same as −2 ≤ x ≤ 3: closed (shaded) dots at −2 and at 3; shade the part of the line between −2 and 3.

Q: 9. 4 < x < 6

Ans: Open circles at 4 and at 6 (neither end value is included); shade the part of the line between 4 and 6.

Q: 10. −3 < x < 0

Ans: Open circles at −3 and at 0 (neither end value is included); shade the part of the line between −3 and 0.

mcqs.q: How is x > 0 depicted on a number line?
options: Closed dot at 0, shade to the right
Open circle at 0, shade to the right
Open circle at 0, shade to the left
Closed dot at 0, shade to the left
mcqs.why: The symbol > means 0 is not included, so an open circle is put at 0. Values greater than 0 lie to the right of 0, so the line is shaded to the right with an arrow showing it continues without end.

mcqs.q: How is x < 0 depicted on a number line?
options: Open circle at 0, shade to the left
Closed dot at 0, shade to the left
Open circle at 0, shade to the right
Closed dot at 0, shade to the right
mcqs.why: The symbol < means 0 is not included, so an open circle is put at 0. Values less than 0 lie to the left of 0, so the line is shaded to the left of 0.

mcqs.q: How is x ≤ 1 depicted on a number line?
options: Open circle at 1, shade to the left
Open circle at 1, shade to the right
Closed dot at 1, shade to the right
Closed dot at 1, shade to the left
mcqs.why: The symbol ≤ includes the end value, so a closed (shaded) dot is put at 1. Values less than or equal to 1 lie to the left of 1, so the line is shaded to the left of 1.

mcqs.q: How is x ≤ −5 depicted on a number line?
options: Closed dot at −5, shade to the left
Closed dot at −5, shade to the right
Open circle at −5, shade to the left
Open circle at 5, shade to the left
mcqs.why: The symbol ≤ includes the end value, so a closed (shaded) dot is put at −5. Values less than or equal to −5 lie further left on the number line, so the shading goes to the left of −5.

mcqs.q: How is x ≥ −3 depicted on a number line?
options: Open circle at −3, shade to the right
Closed dot at −3, shade to the left
Closed dot at −3, shade to the right
Closed dot at 3, shade to the right
mcqs.why: The symbol ≥ includes the end value, so a closed (shaded) dot is put at −3. Values greater than or equal to −3 lie to the right of −3, so the line is shaded to the right.

mcqs.q: How is x ≥ 4 depicted on a number line?
options: Closed dot at 4, shade to the right
Open circle at 4, shade to the right
Closed dot at 4, shade to the left
Open circle at 4, shade to the left
mcqs.why: The symbol ≥ includes the end value, so a closed (shaded) dot is put at 4. Values greater than or equal to 4 lie to the right of 4, so the line is shaded to the right of 4.

mcqs.q: How is −5 ≤ x ≤ 6 depicted on a number line?
options: Open circles at −5 and 6, shade between them
Closed dots at −5 and 6, shade between them
Closed dots at −5 and 6, shade outside them
mcqs.why: Both inequalities are ≤, so both end values −5 and 6 are included and get closed (shaded) dots. x must lie between the two values, so only the part of the line between −5 and 6 is shaded.

mcqs.q: The inequality 3 ≥ x ≥ −2 is the same as:
mcqs.why: Reading 3 ≥ x ≥ −2 from the middle value x outward: x ≤ 3 and x ≥ −2. Written in the usual increasing order this is −2 ≤ x ≤ 3, depicted with closed dots at −2 and at 3 and shading between them.

mcqs.q: How is 4 < x < 6 depicted on a number line?
options: Closed dots at 4 and 6, shade between them
Open circles at 4 and 6, shade between them
Open circles at 4 and 6, shade outside them
Closed dot at 4, open circle at 6
mcqs.why: Both inequalities are strict (<), so neither end value is included: open circles are put at 4 and at 6. x lies strictly between the two values, so the part of the line between 4 and 6 is shaded.

mcqs.q: How is −3 < x < 0 depicted on a number line?
options: Closed dots at −3 and 0, shade between them
Open circle at 0 only, shade to the left
Open circles at −3 and 0, shade between them
Open circles at −3 and 0, shade outside them
mcqs.why: Both inequalities are strict (<), so neither end value is included: open circles are put at −3 and at 0. x lies strictly between −3 and 0, so the part of the line between them is shaded.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.5
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Inequalities are solved like equations (add, subtract, multiply, divide both sides), then the solution set is written for the given domain: N, Z, R or a given finite set.
  • 5x + 4 < 34 with x ∈ N gives x < 6, so the solution set is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.
  • With a given finite set, test which listed values satisfy the final inequality, e.g. 2(x − 3) ≥ x − 2 gives x ≥ 4, and from {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4} only 4 qualifies.
  • Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by the L.C.M of the denominators (6 for halves and thirds).
  • A double inequality is handled in all three parts at once: 5 ≤ x + 2 ≤ 8 gives 3 ≤ x ≤ 6 after subtracting 2 from each part.
  • 5 ≥ x ≥ −2 is rewritten as −2 ≤ x ≤ 5 before depicting it.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Solve: 5x + 4 < 34, x ∈ N

Ans: Subtract 4 from both sides:
5x < 30
Divide both sides by 5:
x < 6
Since x ∈ N = {1, 2, 3, ...}:
Solution set = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

Q: 2. 3x − 5 > 1, x ∈ N

Ans: Add 5 to both sides:
3x > 6
Divide both sides by 3:
x > 2
Since x ∈ N:
Solution set = {3, 4, 5, ...}

Q: 3. 3(x + 4) > x + 5, x ∈ R

Ans: Expand the bracket:
3x + 12 > x + 5
Subtract x from both sides:
2x + 12 > 5
Subtract 12 from both sides:
2x > −7
Divide both sides by 2:
x > −7/2
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and x > −7/2}

Q: 4. 3x − 4 > 2, x ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}

Ans: Add 4 to both sides:
3x > 6
Divide both sides by 3:
x > 2
From the given set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, the values greater than 2 are:
Solution set = {3, 4, 5, 6}

Q: 5. 2(x − 3) ≥ x − 2, x ∈ {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}

Ans: Expand the bracket:
2x − 6 ≥ x − 2
Subtract x from both sides:
x − 6 ≥ −2
Add 6 to both sides:
x ≥ 4
From the given set {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, only 4 satisfies this:
Solution set = {4}

Q: 6. (2x + 6)/2 ≥ (x − 9)/3, x ∈ R

Ans: Multiply both sides by 6 (the L.C.M of 2 and 3):
3(2x + 6) ≥ 2(x − 9)
6x + 18 ≥ 2x − 18
Subtract 2x from both sides:
4x + 18 ≥ −18
Subtract 18 from both sides:
4x ≥ −36
Divide both sides by 4:
x ≥ −9
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and x ≥ −9}

Q: 7. (x − 1)/3 ≤ (1 − x)/2, x ∈ Z

Ans: Multiply both sides by 6 (the L.C.M of 3 and 2):
2(x − 1) ≤ 3(1 − x)
2x − 2 ≤ 3 − 3x
Add 3x to both sides:
5x − 2 ≤ 3
Add 2 to both sides:
5x ≤ 5
Divide both sides by 5:
x ≤ 1
Since x ∈ Z:
Solution set = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1}

Q: 8. Find the solution set and depict it on the number line: −2 < x < 3

Ans: Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and −2 < x < 3}.
On the number line: open circles at −2 and at 3 (neither value is included); shade the part of the line between them.

Q: 9. −4 > x > −8

Ans: −4 > x > −8 is the same as −8 < x < −4.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and −8 < x < −4}.
On the number line: open circles at −8 and at −4; shade the part of the line between them.

Q: 10. 7 ≤ x + 4 ≤ 4 (as printed)

Ans: As printed, the two bounds contradict each other: 7 ≤ x + 4 gives x ≥ 3, while x + 4 ≤ 4 gives x ≤ 0. No value of x satisfies both, so the solution set is empty. (The upper bound 4 appears to be a misprint.)
Solution set = { }

Q: 11. 5 ≥ x ≥ −2

Ans: 5 ≥ x ≥ −2 is the same as −2 ≤ x ≤ 5.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and −2 ≤ x ≤ 5}.
On the number line: closed (shaded) dots at −2 and at 5 (both values are included); shade the part of the line between them.

Q: 12. 5 ≤ x + 2 ≤ 8

Ans: Subtract 2 from all three parts:
5 − 2 ≤ x ≤ 8 − 2
3 ≤ x ≤ 6
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and 3 ≤ x ≤ 6}.
On the number line: closed (shaded) dots at 3 and at 6; shade the part of the line between them.

mcqs.q: Solve: 5x + 4 < 34, x ∈ N. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Subtract 4 from both sides: 5x < 30. Divide both sides by 5: x < 6. Since x ∈ N = {1, 2, 3, ...}, the natural numbers less than 6 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Solution set = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3x − 5 > 1, x ∈ N. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Add 5 to both sides: 3x > 6. Divide both sides by 3: x > 2. Since x ∈ N, the natural numbers greater than 2 are 3, 4, 5, .... Solution set = {3, 4, 5, ...}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3(x + 4) > x + 5, x ∈ R. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Expand the bracket: 3x + 12 > x + 5. Subtract x from both sides: 2x + 12 > 5. Subtract 12 from both sides: 2x > −7. Divide both sides by 2: x > −7/2. Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and x > −7/2}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3x − 4 > 2, x ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Add 4 to both sides: 3x > 6. Divide both sides by 3: x > 2. From the given set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, the values greater than 2 are 3, 4, 5 and 6. Solution set = {3, 4, 5, 6}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2(x − 3) ≥ x − 2, x ∈ {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Expand the bracket: 2x − 6 ≥ x − 2. Subtract x from both sides: x − 6 ≥ −2. Add 6 to both sides: x ≥ 4. From the given set {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, only 4 satisfies x ≥ 4. Solution set = {4}.

mcqs.q: Solve: (2x + 6)/2 ≥ (x − 9)/3, x ∈ R. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by 6, the L.C.M of 2 and 3: 3(2x + 6) ≥ 2(x − 9), so 6x + 18 ≥ 2x − 18. Subtract 2x: 4x + 18 ≥ −18. Subtract 18: 4x ≥ −36. Divide by 4: x ≥ −9. Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and x ≥ −9}.

mcqs.q: Solve: (x − 1)/3 ≤ (1 − x)/2, x ∈ Z. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by 6, the L.C.M of 3 and 2: 2(x − 1) ≤ 3(1 − x), so 2x − 2 ≤ 3 − 3x. Add 3x to both sides: 5x − 2 ≤ 3. Add 2: 5x ≤ 5. Divide by 5: x ≤ 1. Since x ∈ Z, the solution set is {..., −2, −1, 0, 1}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 5 ≤ x + 2 ≤ 8, x ∈ R. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Work on all three parts at once. Subtract 2 from each part: 5 − 2 ≤ x ≤ 8 − 2, giving 3 ≤ x ≤ 6. Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and 3 ≤ x ≤ 6}, depicted with closed dots at 3 and 6 and shading between them.

mcqs.q: The inequality −4 > x > −8 has solution set:
mcqs.why: Rewrite −4 > x > −8 in increasing order: −8 < x < −4, because x is less than −4 and greater than −8. Solution set = {x | x ∈ R and −8 < x < −4}, depicted with open circles at −8 and −4 and shading between them.

mcqs.q: As printed, 7 ≤ x + 4 ≤ 4 has solution set:
mcqs.why: Split the double inequality: 7 ≤ x + 4 gives x ≥ 3, while x + 4 ≤ 4 gives x ≤ 0. No value of x is both ≥ 3 and ≤ 0, so the two bounds contradict each other and the solution set is empty. The upper bound 4 in the printed question appears to be a misprint.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.6 (Objective Type Questions)
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • x/4 = 3 is a linear equation in one variable; a linear equation's solution set has exactly one element.
  • √x + 2 = 4 gives x = 4, not 2; √(x + 5) = 3 gives x = 4; √(5x + 3) + 2 = 4 gives x = 1/5.
  • |x| = −x when x < 0 (for x > 0, |x| = x); |x| − 2 = 0 gives {2, −2} and |−x| = 0 gives {0}.
  • Triangle inequality: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|.
  • Multiplying an inequality by a positive number keeps its direction: if x < y and z > 0, then xz < yz.
  • '≤' means less than or equal to; an inequality has infinitely many solutions, unlike a linear equation.
  • For x ∈ N, −1 ≤ x ≤ 1 gives {1}, and 3x − 2 > 7 gives {4, 5, 6, ...}.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). x/4 = 3 is a linear equation in one variable

Ans: True

Q: Q1 (ii). The solution set of 5x + 3 = 8 is {1}

Ans: True

Q: Q1 (iii). The solution set of √x + 2 = 4 is {2}

Ans: False

Q: Q1 (iv). |x| = −x when x > 0

Ans: False

Q: Q1 (v). If x < y and y < z then x > 0

Ans: False

Q: Q2 (i). If x < y then xz ______ yz, for z > 0

Ans: <

Q: Q2 (ii). '≤' means ______

Ans: less than or equal to

Q: Q2 (iii). The solution set of |x| − 2 = 0 is ______

Ans: {2, −2}

Q: Q2 (iv). The solution set of √(x + 5) = 3 is ______

Ans: {4}

Q: Q2 (v). The solution set of 0 < x + 2 < 3, when x ∈ Z, is ______

Ans: {−1, 0}

Q: Q3 (i). |a + b| ______

Options: (a) = |a| + |b| (b) ≤ |a| + |b| (c) > |a| + |b| (d) ≥ |a| + |b|

Correct answer: ≤ |a| + |b|

Q: Q3 (ii). The solution set of a linear equation has

Options: (a) one element (b) two elements (c) No element (d) infinite number of elements

Correct answer: one element

Q: Q3 (iii). The solution set of √x = −6 is:

Options: (a) {36} (b) {6} (c) {−6} (d) { }

Correct answer: { }

Q: Q3 (iv). √(x + 4) + 2 = 7 is a:

Options: (a) linear equation (b) radical equation (c) cubic equation (d) quadratic equation

Correct answer: radical equation

Q: Q3 (v). The solution of 5 − 3x = −4 is:

Options: (a) {−3} (b) {1, 3} (c) {3} (d) {9}

Correct answer: {3}

Q: Q3 (vi). The solution set of |−x| = 0 is:

Options: (a) {1} (b) {−1} (c) {0} (d) does not exist

Correct answer: {0}

Q: Q3 (vii). x ≤ 5 means:

Options: (a) x > 5 (b) x = 5 (c) x > 5 or x = 5 (d) x < 5 or x = 5

Correct answer: x < 5 or x = 5

Q: Q3 (viii). −5 < 4 means:

Options: (a) −5 lies to the right of 4 (b) −5 lies to the left of 4 (c) −5 coincides with 4 and lies to the left of 4 (d) −5 coincides with 4 and lies to the right of 4

Correct answer: −5 lies to the left of 4

Q: Q3 (ix). The solution set of |4x/3| = 4 is:

Options: (a) {3} (b) {4, −4} (c) 3, −3 } (d) {4, −4}

Correct answer: 3, −3 }

Q: Q3 (x). The solution set of 3x − 2 > 7, x ∈ N is:

Options: (a) {1, 2, 3, ...} (b) {3, 4, 5, ...} (c) {4, 5, 6, ...} (d) {9, 10, 11, ...}

Correct answer: {4, 5, 6, ...}

Q: Q3 (xi). The solution set of −1 ≤ x ≤ 1, x ∈ N is:

Options: (a) {−1, 0, 1} (b) {0} (c) {−1} (d) {1}

Correct answer: {1}

Q: Q3 (xii). The solution set of √(5x + 3) + 2 = 4 is:

Options: (a) {1/5} (b) {−1/5} (c) {2} (d) 1

Correct answer: {1/5}

Q: Q3 (xiii). The symbol '>' means:

Options: (a) less than (b) greater than (c) less than or equal to (d) greater than or equal to

Correct answer: greater than

Q: Q3 (xiv). An inequality has ______ solutions.

Options: (a) finite number of (b) infinite number of (c) two (d) no

Correct answer: infinite number of

Q: Note about the scanned copy (Unit 4)

Ans: Printed pages 86 and 97 are missing from the scanned copy of the textbook used for these notes. Page 86 contains only theory (verification of the properties of absolute value) and page 97 contains only the start of this unit's summary; no exercise question is missing — every exercise of this unit (4.1 to 4.6) is complete above. The answer-key pages for Exercises 4.5 and 4.6 (printed page 324) are also missing from the scan; those answers were worked out in full from the questions.

mcqs.q: True or False: x/4 = 3 is a linear equation in one variable.
mcqs.why: The equation x/4 = 3 contains only one variable, x, and the highest power of x is 1 (x/4 is x divided by 4, i.e. (1/4)x). So it is a linear equation in one variable, and the statement is True.

mcqs.q: True or False: The solution set of 5x + 3 = 8 is {1}.
mcqs.why: Solve: subtract 3 from both sides, 5x = 5; divide both sides by 5, x = 1. Verification: 5(1) + 3 = 8 ✓. So the solution set is {1} and the statement is True.

mcqs.q: True or False: The solution set of √x + 2 = 4 is {2}.
mcqs.why: Solve: subtract 2 from both sides, √x = 2; square both sides, x = 4. Verification: √4 + 2 = 2 + 2 = 4 ✓. The solution set is {4}, not {2}, so the statement is False.

mcqs.q: True or False: |x| = −x when x > 0.
mcqs.why: By definition, |x| = x when x > 0 and |x| = −x when x < 0. For example, |3| = 3, not −3. So the statement as given (for x > 0) is False.

mcqs.q: If x < y, then for z > 0, xz ______ yz. Fill in the blank.
mcqs.why: Multiplying both sides of an inequality by a positive number keeps the direction of the inequality unchanged. Since z > 0 and x < y, multiplying by z gives xz < yz. So the blank is filled by '<'.

mcqs.q: '≤' means:
mcqs.why: The symbol ≤ combines < (less than) with = (equal to): a ≤ b means a is less than b or a is equal to b. So '≤' means 'less than or equal to'.

mcqs.q: The solution set of |x| − 2 = 0 is:
mcqs.why: Add 2 to both sides: |x| = 2. This gives two possibilities, x = 2 or x = −2. So the solution set is {2, −2}.

mcqs.q: The solution set of √(x + 5) = 3 is:
mcqs.why: Square both sides: x + 5 = 3² = 9. Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 4. Verification: √(4 + 5) = √9 = 3 ✓. So the solution set is {4}.

mcqs.q: The solution set of 0 < x + 2 < 3, when x ∈ Z, is:
mcqs.why: Subtract 2 from all three parts: 0 − 2 < x < 3 − 2, so −2 < x < 1. The integers strictly between −2 and 1 are −1 and 0. So the solution set is {−1, 0}.

This is the triangle inequality: the absolute value of a sum is never greater than the sum of the absolute values, |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|. Equality holds only when a and b have the same sign (or one is 0). This is the book's own keyed answer.

mcqs.q: The solution set of a linear equation has:
mcqs.why: A linear equation in one variable reduces to x = a single value, for example 5x + 3 = 8 gives x = 1 only. So its solution set has exactly one element. This is the book's own keyed answer.

mcqs.q: The solution set of √x = −6 is:
mcqs.why: A square root is never negative, so √x = −6 has no solution: squaring would give x = 36, but √36 = 6, not −6, so 36 is an extraneous root. The solution set is { } (empty). This is the book's own keyed answer.
The equation contains the unknown x under a square root sign (a radical), √(x + 4). An equation with the variable under a radical is called a radical equation. This is the book's own keyed answer.

mcqs.q: The solution of 5 − 3x = −4 is:
mcqs.why: Solve step by step: subtract 5 from both sides, −3x = −4 − 5 = −9. Divide both sides by −3: x = (−9)/(−3) = 3. Verification: 5 − 3(3) = 5 − 9 = −4 ✓. So the solution is {3}. This is the book's own keyed answer.

mcqs.q: The solution set of |4x/3| = 4 is:
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: 4x/3 = 4 gives 4x = 12, so x = 3; 4x/3 = −4 gives 4x = −12, so x = −3. So the solution set is {3, −3}. Note: in the book this correct option is printed with a missing opening brace ('3, −3 }'); the intended keyed answer is {3, −3}.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A quadratic equation has degree 2 and standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.
  • x − 6/x + 5 = 0 becomes x² + 5x − 6 = 0 after multiplying by x, so it is quadratic (reducible to quadratic form).
  • 1/x² = 1 becomes x² − 1 = 0, with a = 1, b = 0, c = −1.
  • x² − 1/x + 3 = 0 becomes x³ + 3x − 1 = 0, a cubic, so it is not quadratic.
  • x² = 3x + 1 in standard form is x² − 3x − 1 = 0, so a = 1, b = −3, c = −1.
  • 1/x² − 2 + 3/x = 0 in standard form is 2x² − 3x − 1 = 0.
  • x² − 3 = 0 has b = 0, and 3x² − x = 0 has c = 0; a missing term means its coefficient is 0.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Which of the following are quadratic equations? x² − 1/x + 3 = 0

Ans: Multiply both sides by x to clear the fraction:
x³ + 3x − 1 = 0
The highest power of x is 3, so the equation is cubic, not quadratic.
Not a quadratic equation.

Q: Q1 (ii). x⁴ − 2x + 1 = 0

Ans: The highest power of x is 4.
Not a quadratic equation.

Q: Q1 (iii). x − 6/x + 5 = 0

Ans: Multiply both sides by x to clear the fraction:
x² + 5x − 6 = 0
This is of the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a = 1, b = 5, c = −6.
It is a quadratic equation (reducible to quadratic form).

Q: Q1 (iv). x(2x² + 4) = 0

Ans: Expand the bracket:
2x³ + 4x = 0
The highest power of x is 3, so the equation is cubic.
Not a quadratic equation.

Q: Q1 (v). 1/x² = 1

Ans: Multiply both sides by x²:
1 = x²
x² − 1 = 0
This is of the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a = 1, b = 0, c = −1.
It is a quadratic equation (reducible to quadratic form).

Q: Q1 (vi). x = 0

Ans: The highest power of x is 1; it is a linear equation.
Not a quadratic equation.

Q: Q2 (i). Arrange in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0: x² = 3x + 1

Ans: Bring all terms to the left side:
x² − 3x − 1 = 0
Here a = 1, b = −3, c = −1.

Q: Q2 (ii). 1/x² − 2 + 3/x = 0

Ans: Multiply both sides by x² to clear the fractions:
1 − 2x² + 3x = 0
Multiply by −1 and arrange:
2x² − 3x − 1 = 0
Here a = 2, b = −3, c = −1.

Q: Q2 (iii). x² − 3 = 0

Ans: It is already in standard form:
x² − 3 = 0, i.e. x² + 0x − 3 = 0
Here a = 1, b = 0, c = −3.

Q: Q2 (iv). x² = 5x − 1

Ans: Bring all terms to the left side:
x² − 5x + 1 = 0
Here a = 1, b = −5, c = 1.

Q: Q2 (v). 3x² − x = 0

Ans: It is already in standard form:
3x² − x = 0, i.e. 3x² − x + 0 = 0
Here a = 3, b = −1, c = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the standard form of a quadratic equation?
mcqs.why: A quadratic equation is a polynomial equation of degree 2. Its standard form is ax² + bx + c = 0, and a must not be 0, otherwise the x² term disappears and the equation is no longer quadratic.

mcqs.q: After clearing fractions, x − 6/x + 5 = 0 becomes:
mcqs.why: Multiply every term by x: x × x = x², x × (−6/x) = −6, and x × 5 = 5x. This gives x² + 5x − 6 = 0, which is of the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a = 1, b = 5, c = −6.

mcqs.q: The equation x² − 1/x + 3 = 0 is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by x to clear the fraction: x × x² = x³, x × (−1/x) = −1, x × 3 = 3x, giving x³ + 3x − 1 = 0. The highest power of x is 3, so the equation is cubic, not quadratic.

mcqs.q: The equation 1/x² = 1, written in standard form, is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by x²: x² × (1/x²) = 1 and x² × 1 = x², so 1 = x². Bringing all terms to one side gives x² − 1 = 0, with a = 1, b = 0 and c = −1, so it is quadratic.

mcqs.q: For x² = 3x + 1 written in standard form, the values of a, b and c are:
mcqs.why: Bring all terms to the left side: x² − 3x − 1 = 0. Comparing with ax² + bx + c = 0, the coefficient of x² is a = 1, the coefficient of x is b = −3, and the constant term is c = −1.

mcqs.q: The equation 1/x² − 2 + 3/x = 0 in standard form is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by x²: 1 − 2x² + 3x = 0. Multiply by −1 to make the x² coefficient positive and arrange in descending powers: 2x² − 3x − 1 = 0, so a = 2, b = −3, c = −1.

mcqs.q: In the equation x² − 3 = 0, the coefficient b is:
mcqs.why: Write the equation fully as x² + 0x − 3 = 0. There is no x term, so its coefficient is b = 0, while a = 1 and c = −3. The equation is already in standard form.

mcqs.q: In the equation 3x² − x = 0, the constant term c is:
mcqs.why: Write the equation fully as 3x² − x + 0 = 0. There is no constant term, so c = 0, while a = 3 and b = −1. The equation is already in standard form.

mcqs.q: The equation x(2x² + 4) = 0 is:
options: Quadratic, because of the x outside
Linear, because x = 0 is a solution
Quadratic, because it has two factors
mcqs.why: Expand the bracket: x × 2x² = 2x³ and x × 4 = 4x, giving 2x³ + 4x = 0. The highest power of x is 3, so the equation is cubic, not quadratic, whatever its solutions are.

mcqs.q: The equation x⁴ − 2x + 1 = 0 is not quadratic because:
options: Its highest power of x is 4
It has no x² term shown separately
mcqs.why: The degree of an equation is the highest power of the variable in it. Here the term x⁴ gives degree 4, while a quadratic equation must have degree exactly 2, so this equation is not quadratic.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Factorization uses the zero-factor property: if (x − p)(x − q) = 0 then x = p or x = q.
  • 1 + 15/x² = 16/x clears to x² − 16x + 15 = 0 = (x − 1)(x − 15), giving solution set {1, 15}.
  • A value that makes an original denominator zero must be rejected, even if it solves the cleared equation.
  • 64x² + 16x + 1 = (8x + 1)², so 64x² + 16x = −1 has the repeated root x = −1/8.
  • Completing the square: add the square of half the coefficient of x to both sides to form (x − h)² = k.
  • x² − 2x − 444 = 0 gives (x − 1)² = 445 and roots 1 ± √445.
  • x² = 25x − 24 gives (x − 25/2)² = 529/4 and roots 24 and 1.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Solve by factorization: 1 + 15/x² = 16/x, (x ≠ 0)

Ans: Multiply both sides by x²:
x² + 15 = 16x
x² − 16x + 15 = 0
Two numbers with product 15 and sum −16 are −1 and −15:
x² − x − 15x + 15 = 0
x(x − 1) − 15(x − 1) = 0
(x − 1)(x − 15) = 0
By the zero-factor property: x − 1 = 0 or x − 15 = 0
x = 1 or x = 15
Solution set = {1, 15}

Q: Q1 (ii). x(3x − 5) = (x − 6)(x − 7)

Ans: Expand both sides:
3x² − 5x = x² − 13x + 42
2x² + 8x − 42 = 0
Divide both sides by 2:
x² + 4x − 21 = 0
x² + 7x − 3x − 21 = 0
x(x + 7) − 3(x + 7) = 0
(x + 7)(x − 3) = 0
x = −7 or x = 3
Solution set = {−7, 3}

Q: Q1 (iii). x/(x + 6) + 3/(x + 4) = 6/((x + 6)(x + 4)), (x ≠ −6, −4)

Ans: Multiply both sides by (x + 6)(x + 4):
x(x + 4) + 3(x + 6) = 6
x² + 4x + 3x + 18 = 6
x² + 7x + 12 = 0
(x + 3)(x + 4) = 0
x = −3 or x = −4
But the question states x ≠ −6, −4, because x = −4 makes the original denominators zero. So x = −4 is rejected.
Solution set = {−3}
(The book's answer key lists {−3, −4}, the roots of the cleared equation, but −4 is excluded by the condition given in the question.)

Q: Q1 (iv). 6x + 1/x = 7, x ≠ 0

Ans: Multiply both sides by x:
6x² + 1 = 7x
6x² − 7x + 1 = 0
Here ac = 6; two numbers with product 6 and sum −7 are −6 and −1:
6x² − 6x − x + 1 = 0
6x(x − 1) − 1(x − 1) = 0
(6x − 1)(x − 1) = 0
x = 1/6 or x = 1
Solution set = {1/6, 1}

Q: Q1 (v). 64x² + 16x = −1

Ans: Bring all terms to one side:
64x² + 16x + 1 = 0
64x² + 8x + 8x + 1 = 0
8x(8x + 1) + 1(8x + 1) = 0
(8x + 1)(8x + 1) = 0
(8x + 1)² = 0
x = −1/8
Solution set = {−1/8}

Q: Q2 (i). Solve by completing square: x² − 2x − 444 = 0

Ans: Shift the constant term to the right:
x² − 2x = 444
Add the square of half the coefficient of x, (2/2)² = 1, to both sides:
x² − 2x + 1 = 444 + 1
(x − 1)² = 445
Take square roots:
x − 1 = ±√445
x = 1 ± √445
Solution set = {1 + √445, 1 − √445}

Q: Q2 (ii). 5x² − 10x − 890 = 0

Ans: Divide both sides by 5:
x² − 2x − 178 = 0
x² − 2x = 178
Add (2/2)² = 1 to both sides:
(x − 1)² = 179
x − 1 = ±√179
x = 1 ± √179
Solution set = {1 + √179, 1 − √179}

Q: Q2 (iii). x² − 4x − 921 = 0

Ans: x² − 4x = 921
Add (4/2)² = 4 to both sides:
x² − 4x + 4 = 921 + 4
(x − 2)² = 925
x − 2 = ±√925 = ±5√37
x = 2 ± 5√37
Solution set = {2 + 5√37, 2 − 5√37}

Q: Q2 (iv). x² = 25x − 24

Ans: Write in standard form:
x² − 25x + 24 = 0
x² − 25x = −24
Add (25/2)² = 625/4 to both sides:
(x − 25/2)² = 625/4 − 24 = 529/4
x − 25/2 = ±23/2
x = (25 + 23)/2 = 24 or x = (25 − 23)/2 = 1
Solution set = {24, 1}

Q: Q2 (v). x² − 10x + 10 = 0

Ans: x² − 10x = −10
Add (10/2)² = 25 to both sides:
x² − 10x + 25 = −10 + 25
(x − 5)² = 15
x − 5 = ±√15
x = 5 ± √15
Solution set = {5 + √15, 5 − √15}

Q: Q2 (vi). 2x² = 32x + 34

Ans: Divide both sides by 2:
x² = 16x + 17
x² − 16x = 17
Add (16/2)² = 64 to both sides:
x² − 16x + 64 = 17 + 64
(x − 8)² = 81
x − 8 = ±9
x = 8 + 9 = 17 or x = 8 − 9 = −1
Solution set = {17, −1}

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 1 + 15/x² = 16/x (x ≠ 0). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by x²: x² + 15 = 16x, so x² − 16x + 15 = 0. Two numbers with product 15 and sum −16 are −1 and −15: x² − x − 15x + 15 = x(x − 1) − 15(x − 1) = (x − 1)(x − 15) = 0. By the zero-factor property x = 1 or x = 15.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: x(3x − 5) = (x − 6)(x − 7). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Expand both sides: 3x² − 5x = x² − 13x + 42. Bring all terms left: 2x² + 8x − 42 = 0. Divide by 2: x² + 4x − 21 = 0. Split the middle term: x² + 7x − 3x − 21 = x(x + 7) − 3(x + 7) = (x + 7)(x − 3) = 0, so x = −7 or x = 3.

mcqs.q: Solve: x/(x + 6) + 3/(x + 4) = 6/((x + 6)(x + 4)), with x ≠ −6, −4. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by (x + 6)(x + 4): x(x + 4) + 3(x + 6) = 6, so x² + 7x + 18 = 6 and x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0, giving x = −3 or x = −4. But x = −4 makes the original denominators zero and the question excludes it, so it is rejected. Note: the book's answer key lists {−3, −4}, the roots of the cleared equation, but −4 is excluded by the condition in the question, so the correct solution set is {−3}.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 6x + 1/x = 7 (x ≠ 0). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by x: 6x² + 1 = 7x, so 6x² − 7x + 1 = 0. Here ac = 6; two numbers with product 6 and sum −7 are −6 and −1: 6x² − 6x − x + 1 = 6x(x − 1) − 1(x − 1) = (6x − 1)(x − 1) = 0, so x = 1/6 or x = 1.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 64x² + 16x = −1. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Bring all terms to one side: 64x² + 16x + 1 = 0. Split the middle term: 64x² + 8x + 8x + 1 = 8x(8x + 1) + 1(8x + 1) = (8x + 1)(8x + 1) = (8x + 1)² = 0. Hence 8x + 1 = 0 and x = −1/8, a repeated root.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: x² − 2x − 444 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Shift the constant term: x² − 2x = 444. Half the coefficient of x is 2/2 = 1, and 1² = 1; add 1 to both sides: x² − 2x + 1 = 445, i.e. (x − 1)² = 445. Take square roots: x − 1 = ±√445, so x = 1 ± √445.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: 5x² − 10x − 890 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Divide both sides by 5: x² − 2x − 178 = 0, so x² − 2x = 178. Add the square of half the coefficient of x, (2/2)² = 1, to both sides: (x − 1)² = 179. Take square roots: x − 1 = ±√179, so x = 1 ± √179.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: x² − 4x − 921 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Shift the constant term: x² − 4x = 921. Add (4/2)² = 4 to both sides: x² − 4x + 4 = 925, i.e. (x − 2)² = 925. Since 925 = 25 × 37, √925 = 5√37. Take square roots: x − 2 = ±5√37, so x = 2 ± 5√37.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: x² = 25x − 24. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Write in standard form: x² − 25x + 24 = 0, so x² − 25x = −24. Add (25/2)² = 625/4 to both sides: (x − 25/2)² = 625/4 − 24 = 529/4. Take square roots: x − 25/2 = ±23/2, so x = (25 + 23)/2 = 24 or x = (25 − 23)/2 = 1.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: 2x² = 32x + 34. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Divide both sides by 2: x² = 16x + 17, so x² − 16x = 17. Add (16/2)² = 64 to both sides: x² − 16x + 64 = 81, i.e. (x − 8)² = 81. Take square roots: x − 8 = ±9, so x = 8 + 9 = 17 or x = 8 − 9 = −1.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Quadratic formula: for ax² + bx + c = 0, x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a).
  • x² − 8x + 15 = 0 gives x = (8 ± √4)/2, so the solution set is {5, 3}.
  • 3x² − x = 2 becomes 3x² − x − 2 = 0 and gives solution set {1, −2/3}.
  • 4x² + 3x = 0 has c = 0 and gives solution set {0, −3/4}.
  • 3x(x − 2) + 1 = 0 becomes 3x² − 6x + 1 = 0 and gives roots (3 ± √6)/3.
  • x + 1/(6x) = −5/6 clears to 6x² + 5x + 1 = 0 and gives roots −1/3 and −1/2.
  • Always write the equation in standard form first and read off a, b and c with their signs.

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. Solve by quadratic formula: x² − 8x + 15 = 0

Ans: Compare with ax² + bx + c = 0: a = 1, b = −8, c = 15.
Formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)
x = (8 ± √((−8)² − 4(1)(15)))/(2(1))
= (8 ± √(64 − 60))/2
= (8 ± √4)/2
= (8 ± 2)/2
x = 10/2 = 5 or x = 6/2 = 3
Solution set = {5, 3}

Q: 2. 3x² − x = 2

Ans: Write in standard form: 3x² − x − 2 = 0, so a = 3, b = −1, c = −2.
Formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)
x = (1 ± √((−1)² − 4(3)(−2)))/(2(3))
= (1 ± √(1 + 24))/6
= (1 ± √25)/6
= (1 ± 5)/6
x = 6/6 = 1 or x = −4/6 = −2/3
Solution set = {1, −2/3}

Q: 3. 4x² + 3x = 0

Ans: Here a = 4, b = 3, c = 0.
Formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)
x = (−3 ± √((3)² − 4(4)(0)))/(2(4))
= (−3 ± √9)/8
= (−3 ± 3)/8
x = 0/8 = 0 or x = −6/8 = −3/4
Solution set = {0, −3/4}

Q: 4. 3x(x − 2) + 1 = 0

Ans: Expand: 3x² − 6x + 1 = 0, so a = 3, b = −6, c = 1.
Formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)
x = (6 ± √((−6)² − 4(3)(1)))/(2(3))
= (6 ± √(36 − 12))/6
= (6 ± √24)/6
= (6 ± 2√6)/6
= (3 ± √6)/3
Solution set = {(3 + √6)/3, (3 − √6)/3}

Q: 5. x + 1/(6x) = −5/6; x ≠ 0

Ans: Multiply both sides by 6x:
6x² + 1 = −5x
6x² + 5x + 1 = 0, so a = 6, b = 5, c = 1.
Formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)
x = (−5 ± √((5)² − 4(6)(1)))/(2(6))
= (−5 ± √(25 − 24))/12
= (−5 ± 1)/12
x = −4/12 = −1/3 or x = −6/12 = −1/2
Solution set = {−1/3, −1/2}

Q: 6. (x − 1)(x + 3) = 5(x + 2) − 3

Ans: Expand both sides:
x² + 2x − 3 = 5x + 10 − 3
x² + 2x − 3 = 5x + 7
x² − 3x − 10 = 0, so a = 1, b = −3, c = −10.
Formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)
x = (3 ± √((−3)² − 4(1)(−10)))/(2(1))
= (3 ± √(9 + 40))/2
= (3 ± √49)/2
= (3 ± 7)/2
x = 10/2 = 5 or x = −4/2 = −2
Solution set = {5, −2}

Q: 7. (x − 2)/(x + 2) = (2x − 3)/(x − 1), x ≠ 2, 1

Ans: Cross-multiply:
(x − 2)(x − 1) = (2x − 3)(x + 2)
x² − 3x + 2 = 2x² + x − 6
0 = x² + 4x − 8
x² + 4x − 8 = 0, so a = 1, b = 4, c = −8.
Formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)
x = (−4 ± √((4)² − 4(1)(−8)))/(2(1))
= (−4 ± √(16 + 32))/2
= (−4 ± √48)/2
= (−4 ± 4√3)/2
= −2 ± 2√3
Solution set = {−2 + 2√3, −2 − 2√3}

mcqs.q: Solve by the quadratic formula: x² − 8x + 15 = 0. The solution set is:
Solve by the quadratic formula: 3x² − x = 2. The solution set is:
Solve by the quadratic formula: 4x² + 3x = 0. The solution set is:
Solve by the quadratic formula: 3x(x − 2) + 1 = 0. The solution set is:
Solve by the quadratic formula: x + 1/(6x) = −5/6 (x ≠ 0). The solution set is:
Solve by the quadratic formula: (x − 1)(x + 3) = 5(x + 2) − 3. The solution set is:
Solve by the quadratic formula: (x − 2)/(x + 2) = (2x − 3)/(x − 1). The solution set is:
For x² − 8x + 15 = 0, the value under the square root in the quadratic formula, b² − 4ac, is:
mcqs.why: Here a = 1, b = −8, c = 15. Compute step by step: b² = (−8)² = 64, and 4ac = 4 × 1 × 15 = 60. So b² − 4ac = 64 − 60 = 4, and √4 = 2 is what is used in x = (8 ± 2)/2.

mcqs.q: The quadratic formula for ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0) is:
mcqs.why: The quadratic formula is x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a). The numerator starts with −b, the discriminant inside the root is b² − 4ac with a minus sign, and the whole numerator is divided by 2a. Every solution in this exercise is obtained by substituting a, b and c into exactly this formula.

mcqs.q: For the cleared equation 6x² + 5x + 1 = 0, the value b² − 4ac is:
mcqs.why: Here a = 6, b = 5, c = 1. Compute step by step: b² = 5² = 25, and 4ac = 4 × 6 × 1 = 24. So b² − 4ac = 25 − 24 = 1, and the formula gives x = (−5 ± √1)/12 = (−5 ± 1)/12, i.e. −1/3 or −1/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Word problems are solved by choosing a variable, forming a quadratic equation, solving it, and rejecting values impossible in the situation (such as a negative length).
  • For the 460 m² plot with length 12 m more than breadth: b(b + 12) = 460, giving breadth −6 + 4√31 m and length 6 + 4√31 m.
  • A number whose sum with its reciprocal is 2 satisfies (x − 1)² = 0, so the number is 1.
  • A board of area 12 m² with length 1 m more than width has width 3 m and length 4 m.
  • If s² = 4s for a side length s, then s = 4 units (s = 0 is rejected).
  • Two consecutive integers with product 20 are 4 and 5, or −5 and −4.
  • Two integers with product −8 differing by 6 are (2, −4) or (4, −2).

Solved Exercises

Q: 1. The area of a rectangular plot is 460 square meter. The length of the plot is 12 meter more than its breadth. Find the length and breadth of the plot.

Ans: Let the breadth be b metres; the length is (b + 12) metres.
Area = length × breadth:
b(b + 12) = 460
b² + 12b − 460 = 0
Formula: b = (−12 ± √(144 − 4(1)(−460)))/2
= (−12 ± √(144 + 1840))/2
= (−12 ± √1984)/2
= (−12 ± 8√31)/2
= −6 ± 4√31
Breadth cannot be negative, so b = −6 + 4√31 metres.
Length = b + 12 = 6 + 4√31 metres.

Q: 2. The sum of a positive number and its reciprocal is 2. Find the number.

Ans: Let the number be x; its reciprocal is 1/x.
x + 1/x = 2
Multiply both sides by x:
x² + 1 = 2x
x² − 2x + 1 = 0
(x − 1)² = 0
x = 1
The number is 1.

Q: 3. The area of a board in a classroom is 12 square meters. If the length is 1 meter greater than its width, then find out the dimensions of the board.

Ans: Let the width be w metres; the length is (w + 1) metres.
w(w + 1) = 12
w² + w − 12 = 0
(w + 4)(w − 3) = 0
w = 3 or w = −4
Width cannot be negative, so width = 3 metres and length = 3 + 1 = 4 metres.

Q: 4. If the square of the lengths of an equilateral triangle is 4 times the length of its one side. What will be the length of each side?

Ans: Let the length of each side be s.
Square of the side = 4 times the side:
s² = 4s
s² − 4s = 0
s(s − 4) = 0
s = 0 or s = 4
A side cannot be 0, so the length of each side is 4 units.

Q: 5. The product of two consecutive integers is 20. Find the integers.

Ans: Let the first integer be x; the next consecutive integer is x + 1.
x(x + 1) = 20
x² + x − 20 = 0
(x + 5)(x − 4) = 0
x = 4 or x = −5
The integers are 4 and 5, or −5 and −4.

Q: 6. Find two integers if their product is −8 and one integer is 6 less than the other.

Ans: Let the larger integer be x; the other is x − 6.
x(x − 6) = −8
x² − 6x + 8 = 0
(x − 2)(x − 4) = 0
x = 2 or x = 4
If x = 2, the other integer is −4; if x = 4, the other is −2.
The two integers are (2, −4) or (4, −2).

mcqs.q: A rectangular plot has area 460 m² and its length is 12 m more than its breadth. The breadth is:
mcqs.why: Let the breadth be b; the length is b + 12. Area: b(b + 12) = 460, so b² + 12b − 460 = 0. By the formula: b = (−12 ± √(144 − 4(1)(−460)))/2 = (−12 ± √(144 + 1840))/2 = (−12 ± √1984)/2 = (−12 ± 8√31)/2 = −6 ± 4√31. Breadth cannot be negative, so b = −6 + 4√31 metres.

mcqs.q: For the same 460 m² plot (length 12 m more than breadth), the length is:
mcqs.why: From the breadth b = −6 + 4√31 metres (found by solving b² + 12b − 460 = 0 and rejecting the negative root), the length is b + 12 = (−6 + 4√31) + 12 = 6 + 4√31 metres. Check: length − breadth = 12 m, as required.

mcqs.q: The sum of a positive number and its reciprocal is 2. The number is:
mcqs.why: Let the number be x; its reciprocal is 1/x. Then x + 1/x = 2. Multiply both sides by x: x² + 1 = 2x, so x² − 2x + 1 = 0, i.e. (x − 1)² = 0. Hence x = 1. Check: 1 + 1/1 = 2, correct.

mcqs.q: A classroom board has area 12 m² and its length is 1 m greater than its width. Its dimensions are:
mcqs.why: Let the width be w; the length is w + 1. Area: w(w + 1) = 12, so w² + w − 12 = 0 = (w + 4)(w − 3). Hence w = 3 or w = −4. Width cannot be negative, so width = 3 m and length = 3 + 1 = 4 m.

mcqs.q: The square of the side of an equilateral triangle is 4 times the side. The length of each side is:
mcqs.why: Let each side be s. Then s² = 4s, so s² − 4s = 0 and s(s − 4) = 0, giving s = 0 or s = 4. A side cannot be 0, so the length of each side is 4 units.

mcqs.q: The product of two consecutive integers is 20. The positive pair is:
mcqs.why: Let the first integer be x; the next is x + 1. Then x(x + 1) = 20, so x² + x − 20 = 0 = (x + 5)(x − 4), giving x = 4 or x = −5. For x = 4 the pair is 4 and 5, and indeed 4 × 5 = 20.

mcqs.q: The product of two consecutive integers is 20. The negative pair is:
mcqs.why: Solving x(x + 1) = 20 gives x² + x − 20 = (x + 5)(x − 4) = 0, so x = 4 or x = −5. For x = −5 the next consecutive integer is x + 1 = −4, and (−5) × (−4) = 20, so the negative pair is −5 and −4.

mcqs.q: Two integers have product −8 and one is 6 less than the other. The pairs are:
mcqs.why: Let the larger integer be x; the other is x − 6. Then x(x − 6) = −8, so x² − 6x + 8 = 0 = (x − 2)(x − 4), giving x = 2 or x = 4. If x = 2 the other integer is 2 − 6 = −4; if x = 4 it is 4 − 6 = −2. Both pairs have product −8 and differ by 6.

mcqs.q: For the 460 m² plot with length 12 m more than its breadth b, the correct equation is:
mcqs.why: Area of a rectangle = length × breadth. The length is b + 12, so the area equation is b(b + 12) = 460. Expanding gives b² + 12b = 460, and bringing 460 to the left gives b² + 12b − 460 = 0, the equation solved by the quadratic formula in this exercise.

mcqs.q: For the board of area 12 m² with length 1 m greater than width w, the correct equation is:
mcqs.why: Area = length × width. The length is w + 1, so w(w + 1) = 12. Expanding gives w² + w = 12, and bringing 12 to the left gives w² + w − 12 = 0, which factorises as (w + 4)(w − 3) = 0.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.5 (Objective Type Questions)
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The degree of a quadratic equation is 2.
  • In ax² + bx + c = 0 the coefficient a cannot be 0; a = 0 would make the equation linear.
  • The square of a number is never negative; it is positive or zero.
  • Zero-factor property: if a product of two factors is zero, then at least one factor is zero.
  • A quadratic equation is solved by three methods and can be factorised into two linear factors.
  • The formula used to solve a quadratic equation is called the quadratic formula, and the values satisfying the equation are called its roots.
  • One root of x² − 5x + 4 = 0 is 1 (the other is 4); 'quad' means square; x² − 2x + 1 = 0 has two roots counting the repeated root.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). The degree of a quadratic equation is 2

Ans: True

Q: Q1 (ii). In the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, a = 0

Ans: False

Q: Q1 (iii). The square of a number is always negative

Ans: False

Q: Q1 (iv). If the product of two factors is zero, then each factor equal to zero

Ans: True

Q: Q1 (v). The general quadratic equation contains three terms

Ans: True

Q: Q2 (i). A quadratic equation is solved by ______ methods

Ans: three

Q: Q2 (ii). A quadratic equation can be factorized into ______ factors

Ans: two

Q: Q2 (iii). The formula used for solution of a quadratic equation is called ______

Ans: quadratic formula

Q: Q2 (iv). The values of variable which satisfy the quadratic equation are called ______

Ans: roots

Q: Q3 (i). One root of the equation x² − 5x + 4 = 0 is

Options: (a) 0 (b) 1 (c) −1 (d) −4

Correct answer: 1

Q: Q3 (ii). The degree of the quadratic equation is

Options: (a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 4 (d) 1/4

Correct answer: 2

Q: Q3 (iii). Number of roots for the equation x² − 2x + 1 = 0

Options: (a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 0 (d) 3

Correct answer: 2

Q: Q3 (iv). Quad means ______

Options: (a) One (b) Square (c) Three (d) four

Correct answer: Square

Q: Q3 (v). One root of x² − 2x = 0 is ______

Options: (a) 1 (b) 3 (c) −3 (d) 2

Correct answer: 2

mcqs.q: The degree of a quadratic equation is:
mcqs.why: The degree of an equation is the highest power of the variable. A quadratic equation contains x² as its highest power, as in ax² + bx + c = 0, so its degree is 2. This is the book's own objective question, keyed to 2.

mcqs.q: In the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the coefficient a must satisfy:
mcqs.why: If a were 0, the term ax² would vanish and the equation would become the linear equation bx + c = 0. For the equation to stay quadratic, a must be non-zero. The book's true/false statement 'a = 0' is therefore False.

mcqs.q: The square of a real number is:
mcqs.why: Squaring multiplies a number by itself: a positive number gives a positive square, a negative number also gives a positive square, and 0 gives 0. So a square is never negative. The book's statement 'the square of a number is always negative' is False.

mcqs.q: If the product of two factors is zero, then:
options: At least one factor is zero
mcqs.why: This is the zero-factor property used in factorization: if p × q = 0 then p = 0 or q = 0 (or both). It is why, from (x − 1)(x − 15) = 0, we set each factor equal to zero separately to get x = 1 or x = 15.

mcqs.q: A quadratic equation is solved by how many methods (as counted in this unit)?
mcqs.why: The unit teaches three methods for solving a quadratic equation: factorization, completing the square, and the quadratic formula — one exercise of this unit is devoted to each method. This is the book's fill-in-the-blank answer: three.

mcqs.q: A quadratic equation can be factorised into how many linear factors?
mcqs.why: A quadratic is a degree-2 expression, so it splits into two linear factors, for example x² − 16x + 15 = (x − 1)(x − 15). Setting each of the two factors equal to zero gives the two roots. This is the book's fill-in-the-blank answer: two.

mcqs.q: The formula used for the solution of a quadratic equation is called the:
mcqs.why: The formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a) used throughout Exercise 5.3 is called the quadratic formula. This is the book's fill-in-the-blank answer: quadratic formula.

mcqs.q: The values of the variable which satisfy a quadratic equation are called its:
mcqs.why: A value that makes the equation true when substituted for the variable is called a root (or solution) of the equation. For example 1 and 15 are the roots of x² − 16x + 15 = 0. This is the book's fill-in-the-blank answer: roots.

mcqs.q: One root of the equation x² − 5x + 4 = 0 is:
mcqs.why: Factorise: x² − 5x + 4 = (x − 1)(x − 4) = 0, so the roots are x = 1 and x = 4. Check x = 1: 1 − 5 + 4 = 0, correct. This is the book's own MCQ, whose keyed answer is 1.

mcqs.q: 'Quad' means:
mcqs.why: 'Quad' refers to a square — a quadratic equation is named for the squared term x² that defines it. This is the book's own MCQ, whose keyed answer is 'Square'.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Order of a matrix = number of rows × number of columns.
  • A = [0 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9] has 3 rows and 3 columns, so its order is 3-by-3.
  • B = [a b; c d; e f] has order 3-by-2; C = [1 −2 3; 5 6 7] has order 2-by-3; D = [6 7; 0 −2] has order 2-by-2.
  • Two matrices are equal only if they have the same order and every pair of corresponding elements is equal.
  • [6 7 8] (order 1-by-3) and [6; 7; 8] (order 3-by-1) are not equal because their orders differ.
  • [8 0; 4 1] equals [16/2, 1 − 1; 8/2, 2 − 1] because the second simplifies to [8 0; 4 1].

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Write the rows and columns of A = [0 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9]

Ans: Rows: [0 2 3], [4 5 6], [7 8 9] — there are 3 rows.
Columns: [0; 4; 7], [2; 5; 8], [3; 6; 9] — there are 3 columns.

Q: Q1 (ii). B = [a b; c d; e f]

Ans: Rows: [a b], [c d], [e f] — there are 3 rows.
Columns: [a; c; e], [b; d; f] — there are 2 columns.

Q: Q1 (iii). C = [1 −2 3; 5 6 7]

Ans: Rows: [1 −2 3], [5 6 7] — there are 2 rows.
Columns: [1; 5], [−2; 6], [3; 7] — there are 3 columns.

Q: Q1 (iv). D = [6 7; 0 −2]

Ans: Rows: [6 7], [0 −2] — there are 2 rows.
Columns: [6; 0], [7; −2] — there are 2 columns.

Q: Q2 (i). Determine the order of A = [0 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9]

Ans: Order = number of rows × number of columns = 3 × 3.
The order of A is 3-by-3.

Q: Q2 (ii). Order of B = [a b; c d; e f]

Ans: B has 3 rows and 2 columns.
The order of B is 3-by-2.

Q: Q2 (iii). Order of C = [1 −2 3; 5 6 7]

Ans: C has 2 rows and 3 columns.
The order of C is 2-by-3.

Q: Q2 (iv). Order of D = [6 7; 0 −2]

Ans: D has 2 rows and 2 columns.
The order of D is 2-by-2.

Q: Q3 (i). Which pairs are equal? [2 3; 0 4] and [2 3; 0 4]

Ans: Both matrices have the same order (2-by-2) and every pair of corresponding elements is equal (2 = 2, 3 = 3, 0 = 0, 4 = 4).
The pair is equal.

Q: Q3 (ii). [5 2; 1 3] and [2 1; 3 5]

Ans: The orders are the same, but the corresponding elements are not equal: 5 ≠ 2, 2 ≠ 1, 1 ≠ 3, 3 ≠ 5.
The pair is not equal.

Q: Q3 (iii). [6 3; 1 5] and [1 + 5, 4 − 1; 2 − 1, 3 + 1]

Ans: Simplify the second matrix: [1 + 5, 4 − 1; 2 − 1, 3 + 1] = [6 3; 1 4].
Compare with [6 3; 1 5]: the last elements differ, 5 ≠ 4.
The pair is not equal.

Q: Q3 (iv). [6 7 8] and [6; 7; 8]

Ans: The first matrix has order 1-by-3 (one row) and the second has order 3-by-1 (one column). The orders are different.
The pair is not equal.

Q: Q3 (v). [8 0; 4 1] and [16/2, 1 − 1; 8/2, 2 − 1]

Ans: Simplify the second matrix: [16/2, 1 − 1; 8/2, 2 − 1] = [8 0; 4 1].
This is exactly the first matrix, so corresponding elements are equal.
The pair is equal.

mcqs.q: The order of A = [0 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9] is:
mcqs.why: Count the rows and columns: the rows are [0 2 3], [4 5 6], [7 8 9] — 3 rows; the columns are [0; 4; 7], [2; 5; 8], [3; 6; 9] — 3 columns. Order = rows × columns = 3 × 3, i.e. 3-by-3.

mcqs.q: The order of B = [a b; c d; e f] is:
mcqs.why: The rows are [a b], [c d], [e f] — 3 rows. The columns are [a; c; e], [b; d; f] — 2 columns. Order = rows × columns = 3 × 2, i.e. 3-by-2.

mcqs.q: The order of C = [1 −2 3; 5 6 7] is:
mcqs.why: The rows are [1 −2 3], [5 6 7] — 2 rows. The columns are [1; 5], [−2; 6], [3; 7] — 3 columns. Order = rows × columns = 2 × 3, i.e. 2-by-3.

mcqs.q: The order of D = [6 7; 0 −2] is:
mcqs.why: The rows are [6 7], [0 −2] — 2 rows. The columns are [6; 0], [7; −2] — 2 columns. Order = rows × columns = 2 × 2, i.e. 2-by-2.

mcqs.q: How many rows does A = [0 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9] have?
mcqs.why: A row runs horizontally. Reading across, the rows are [0 2 3] (first row), [4 5 6] (second row) and [7 8 9] (third row), so the matrix has exactly 3 rows — and also 3 columns.

mcqs.q: Two matrices are equal when:
options: They contain the same numbers in any positions
They have the same number of elements only
They have the same order and all corresponding elements are equal
One is the transpose of the other
mcqs.why: Equality of matrices needs both conditions together: first the orders must be the same, and then every element in one matrix must equal the element in the same position in the other matrix. If either condition fails, the matrices are not equal.

mcqs.q: The pair [5 2; 1 3] and [2 1; 3 5] is:
options: Not equal, because corresponding elements differ
Not equal, because their orders differ
mcqs.why: The orders are the same (both 2-by-2), but corresponding elements are not equal: position by position, 5 ≠ 2, 2 ≠ 1, 1 ≠ 3 and 3 ≠ 5. Containing the same numbers in different positions is not enough, so the pair is not equal.

options: Not equal, because the (2,2) elements differ: 5 ≠ 4
Not equal, because the orders differ
Equal after changing 5 to 4 in the first matrix only by mistake
mcqs.why: Simplify the second matrix element by element: [1 + 5, 4 − 1; 2 − 1, 3 + 1] = [6 3; 1 4]. Compare with [6 3; 1 5]: the first three corresponding elements match, but the last elements differ, 5 ≠ 4, so the pair is not equal.

mcqs.q: The pair [6 7 8] and [6; 7; 8] is:
options: Equal, because they have the same elements
Not equal, because their orders differ (1-by-3 versus 3-by-1)
Not equal, because 8 is in a different row
mcqs.why: The first matrix [6 7 8] has one row and three columns, order 1-by-3. The second [6; 7; 8] has three rows and one column, order 3-by-1. Equal matrices must first have the same order; since the orders differ, the pair is not equal.

options: Not equal, because the second is written with fractions
Equal, because the second simplifies to [8 0; 4 1]
Not equal, because 16/2 is not an element
Equal only in the first row
mcqs.why: Simplify each element of the second matrix: 16/2 = 8, 1 − 1 = 0, 8/2 = 4, 2 − 1 = 1, giving [8 0; 4 1]. This is exactly the first matrix, the orders are the same and all corresponding elements are equal, so the pair is equal.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A row matrix has only one row; a column matrix has only one column.
  • A square matrix has rows = columns; any other matrix is rectangular. [3] is a square matrix of order 1.
  • A zero (null) matrix has every element 0, e.g. [0], [0 0 0] and [0; 0; 0].
  • A diagonal matrix has all off-diagonal elements 0; a scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are all equal; a unit (identity) matrix is a scalar matrix with diagonal elements all 1.
  • Every unit matrix is scalar and diagonal; every scalar matrix is diagonal; a diagonal matrix need not be scalar.
  • The transpose A' is found by interchanging rows and columns; the identity matrix is unchanged by transposing.
  • A is symmetric if A' = A, and skew-symmetric if A' = −A; every diagonal element of a skew-symmetric matrix must be 0.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1 (i). Identify the row matrices: [1 2; 0 2]

Ans: It has 2 rows and 2 columns — not a row matrix.

Q: Q1 (ii). [1 2 4]

Ans: It has only one row — it is a row matrix.

Q: Q1 (iii). [3; 0; 2]

Ans: It has only one column (3 rows) — it is a column matrix, not a row matrix.

Q: Q1 (iv). [1 2 8; 0 1 3]

Ans: It has 2 rows — not a row matrix.

Q: Q1 (v). [0 4 9]

Ans: It has only one row — it is a row matrix.
So the row matrices in Q1 are (ii) and (v).

Q: Q2 (i). Identify the column matrices: [1 3 0]

Ans: It has only one row — it is a row matrix, not a column matrix.

Q: Q2 (ii). [1 0; 2 1; 3 4]

Ans: It has 2 columns — not a column matrix.

Q: Q2 (iii). [1; 4; 7]

Ans: It has only one column — it is a column matrix.

Q: Q2 (iv). [1 0; 2 3; 8 7]

Ans: It has 2 columns — not a column matrix.

Q: Q2 (v). [0; 7; 1]

Ans: It has only one column — it is a column matrix.
So the column matrices in Q2 are (iii) and (v).

Q: Q3 (i). Identify square and rectangular matrices: [1 2; 3 4; 5 6]

Ans: Rows = 3, Columns = 2; rows ≠ columns — rectangular matrix.

Q: Q3 (ii). [1 2 0; 0 3 1; 4 0 5]

Ans: Rows = 3, Columns = 3; rows = columns — square matrix.

Q: Q3 (iii). [1 0 4; 3 2 0]

Ans: Rows = 2, Columns = 3 — rectangular matrix.

Q: Q3 (iv). [1 2; 3 0; 0 0]

Ans: Rows = 3, Columns = 2 — rectangular matrix.

Q: Q3 (v). [1 2 7; 7 0 1; 1 2 8]

Ans: Rows = 3, Columns = 3 — square matrix.

Q: Q3 (vi). [0 3]

Ans: Rows = 1, Columns = 2 — rectangular matrix.

Q: Q3 (vii). [3]

Ans: Rows = 1, Columns = 1 — square matrix (of order 1).

Q: Q3 (viii). [1; 2]

Ans: Rows = 2, Columns = 1 — rectangular matrix.

Q: Q3 (ix). [2 0 0; 0 2 0; 0 0 2]

Ans: Rows = 3, Columns = 3 — square matrix.

Q: Q3 (x). [1 2 0; 0 3 5]

Ans: Rows = 2, Columns = 3 — rectangular matrix.
Square matrices in Q3: (ii), (v), (vii), (ix). Rectangular matrices: (i), (iii), (iv), (vi), (viii), (x).

Q: Q4 (i). Which are zero/null matrices? [0 0 1; 0 0 0; 0 0 0]

Ans: One element (the top-right) is 1, not 0 — not a zero matrix.

Q: Q4 (ii). [0]

Ans: The only element is 0 — it is a zero (null) matrix.

Q: Q4 (iii). [0 0 0; 0 0 0; 0 0 0]

Ans: Every element is 0 — zero (null) matrix.

Q: Q4 (iv). [0 0 0; 0 1 0; 0 0 0]

Ans: The middle element is 1, not 0 — not a zero matrix.

Q: Q4 (v). [0 0 0]

Ans: Every element is 0 — zero (null) matrix.

Q: Q4 (vi). [0; 0; 0]

Ans: Every element is 0 — zero (null) matrix.

Q: Q4 (vii). [0 0 0; 0 0 0; 0 0 1]

Ans: The last element is 1, not 0 — not a zero matrix.
So the zero matrices in Q4 are (ii), (iii), (v) and (vi).

Q: Q5 (i). Separate scalar, unit and diagonal matrices: [1 0; 0 2]

Ans: Off-diagonal elements are 0, but the diagonal elements 1 and 2 are not all equal — diagonal matrix only (not scalar, not unit).

Q: Q5 (ii). [1 0 0; 0 1 0; 0 0 2]

Ans: Diagonal elements are 1, 1, 2 — not all equal, and not all 1 — diagonal matrix only.

Q: Q5 (iii). [1 0 0; 0 1 0; 0 0 1]

Ans: It is the identity matrix: diagonal elements are all 1 and the rest are 0 — unit matrix. It is also scalar (all diagonal entries equal) and diagonal.

Q: Q5 (iv). [3 0 0; 0 3 0; 0 0 3]

Ans: Diagonal elements are all 3 (equal) with zeros elsewhere — scalar matrix, and also a diagonal matrix. Not a unit matrix.

Q: Q5 (v). [a 0 0; 0 a 0; 0 0 a]

Ans: Diagonal elements are all a (equal) with zeros elsewhere — scalar matrix, and also a diagonal matrix.

Q: Q5 (vi). [0 0 0; 0 6 0; 0 0 6]

Ans: Off-diagonal elements are 0, so it is a diagonal matrix. The diagonal elements 0, 6, 6 are not all equal — not scalar, not unit.

Q: Q5 (vii). [1 0; 0 1]

Ans: It is the 2-by-2 identity matrix — unit matrix; also scalar and diagonal.

Q: Q5 (viii). [2 0; 0 2]

Ans: Diagonal elements are both 2 (equal) with zeros elsewhere — scalar matrix, and also diagonal. Not a unit matrix.
Summary of Q5 — Scalar: (iii), (iv), (v), (vii), (viii); Unit: (iii), (vii); Diagonal: all of (i) to (viii).

Q: Q6 (i). Find the transpose of [1 2; 5 7]

Ans: Interchange rows and columns: the rows [1 2] and [5 7] become the columns.
Transpose = [1 5; 2 7]

Q: Q6 (ii). Transpose of [0 1 3; 3 3 0; 4 5 0]
